ranges.Struthio molybdophanes: desert to savanna plains of northeastern Africa, from northern Ethiopia, Djibouti, and Somalia southward through far southeastern South Sudan, and southeastern Kenya
ranges.Struthio camelus: desert to savanna plains of sub-Saharan Africa (except northeast), in Sahel zone (rare in west), east through Eritrea, southward to Tanzania, and in southern Africa from southern Angola eastward to northern Zimbabwe and through the Cape region
ranges.Dromaius novaehollandiae: grassland to woodland of Australia (except west-central); formerly including Kangaroo and King islands and Tasmania
ranges.Casuarius unappendiculatus: lowlands of New Guinea, including Raja Ampat Islands (off western New Guinea) and Yapen (Cenderawasih Bay, off northwestern New Guinea)
ranges.Casuarius casuarius: New Guinea, including Aru Islands (off southwestern New Guinea) and northeastern Australia (northern Cape York Peninsula)
ranges.Casuarius bennetti: New Guinea, including Yapen (Cenderawasih Bay, off northwestern New Guinea), and New Britain
ranges.Apteryx owenii: Kapiti, South, and formerly North islands (New Zealand)
ranges.Apteryx maxima: montane forest of northwestern South Island (New Zealand)
ranges.Apteryx australis: southwestern South Island and Stewart Island (New Zealand)
ranges.Apteryx rowi: Okarito Forest (west coast of South Island, New Zealand)
ranges.Rhea pennata: puna and steppe of central Andes from southeastern Peru to northern Chile and Patagonian steppes to southern Chile and southern Argentina
ranges.Rhea americana: pampas of east-central South America from eastern Bolivia and northeastern Brazil southward to Río Negro (central Argentina)
ranges.Tinamotis pentlandii: Andes of Peru to northern Bolivia, Chile and northwestern Argentina
ranges.Tinamotis ingoufi: savanna of southwestern Argentina and southern Chile
ranges.Eudromia formosa: dry Chaco scrub of southeastern Bolivia and western Paraguay to Santiago del Estero (northwestern Argentina)
ranges.Eudromia elegans: dry scrub of plains of northern Argentina from Salta in the northwest eastward through Buenos Aires province, southward through Patagonia (including southeastern Chile) to Strait of Magellan, southern Santa Cruz province (southern Argentina)
ranges.Taoniscus nanus: interior southeastern Brazil and northeastern Argentina (Misiones)
ranges.Nothura boraquira: northeastern Brazil to eastern Bolivia and northeastern Paraguay
ranges.Nothura minor: semiarid grassland and scrub of interior southeastern Brazil and east-central Paraguay
ranges.Nothura darwinii: drier open habitats in Andes of south-central Peru to northern Chile and east of Andes to eastern Chubut (central Argentina)
ranges.Nothura maculosa: grassland and fields in lowlands of northeastern Brazil from Maranhão through far northeastern Brazil and southward through northern Río Negro (central Argentina)
ranges.Rhynchotus maculicollis: Andes of northwestern Bolivia to northwestern Argentina
ranges.Rhynchotus rufescens: grassland to wooded savanna of lowlands and plateaux of southern Amazonia to central Argentina, from far eastern Peru (Pampas del Heath), northeastward to Maranhão and far northeastern Brazil, southward through La Pampa and southern Buenos Aires province (east-central Argentina)
ranges.Nothoprocta cinerascens: Chaco dry forest in lowlands and plateaus of southeastern Bolivia to northeastern Río Negro (central Argentina)
ranges.Nothoprocta curvirostris: puna and páramo of high Andes from far southwestern Colombia to central Peru
ranges.Nothoprocta ornata: high Andes from north-central Peru through Jujuy and La Rioja (northwestern Argentina)
ranges.Nothoprocta taczanowskii: Andes of south-central Peru (Junín to Puno)
ranges.Nothoprocta perdicaria: grassland and cultivation of lowlands to mountains of north-central to south-central Chile; introduced to Easter Island
ranges.Nothoprocta pentlandii: scrub of hills to high Andes from south-central Ecuador to Mendoza (north-central Argentina)
ranges.Nothocercus julius: Andes of central Colombia and far western Venezuela; also south-central Peru
ranges.Nothocercus nigrocapillus: Andes of northwestern Peru to central Bolivia
ranges.Nothocercus bonapartei: mountains of Costa Rica and Panama, and Andes from Venezuela to northern Peru
ranges.Tinamus major: lowlands of southeastern Mexico through Amazonia and the Guiana Shield
ranges.Tinamus guttatus: southeastern Colombia and southern Venezuela to northern Bolivia and Amazonian Brazil
ranges.Tinamus osgoodi: Andes of south-central Colombia to southeastern Peru
ranges.Tinamus solitarius: eastern Brazil to southeastern Paraguay and far northeastern Argentina (Misiones)
ranges.Tinamus tao: lowland, hill, and gallery forest of northern South America north of the Amazon River, the east slope of the Andes from northern Colombia to central Peru, and in south-central and southern Amazonia from central Bolivia northeast through western Maranhão (north-central Brazil)
ranges.Crypturellus resonans: Sierra del Divisor, Loreto, Peru, and Serra do Divisor, Acre, Brazil
ranges.Crypturellus berlepschi: tropical forest of northwestern Colombia to northwestern Ecuador
ranges.Crypturellus cinereus: southeastern Colombia to the Guianas, southern Venezuela, northern Bolivia, and northeastern Brazil
ranges.Crypturellus ptaritepui: tepuis of southern Venezuela (Ptari-tepui and Sororopán-tepui)
ranges.Crypturellus obsoletus: humid to dry forest of lowlands and hills of northern and central South America (except northern and central Amazonia), with disjunct populations in northern Venezuela, eastern Andes of Colombia and Ecuador (where poorly known), through southwestern Amazonia to central Bolivia and northeastward to northern Pará; also eastern Brazil from Bahia southward through eastern Paraguay and far northern Uruguay
ranges.Crypturellus parvirostris: patchily distributed in Amazon basin southward to northeastern Argentina
ranges.Crypturellus tataupa: forest and edge in lowlands to hills of far southeastern Ecuador on east side of Andes eastward to Maranhão and far northeastern Brazil, and southward to San Luis (northwestern Argentina) and Rio Grande do Sul (far southeastern Brazil)
ranges.Crypturellus variegatus: Colombia to Venezuela, the Guianas, northern Bolivia, and Amazonian Brazil
ranges.Crypturellus soui: lowlands and hills of southern Mexico through southern Brazil
ranges.Crypturellus bartletti: tropical western Amazonian Brazil, eastern Peru, and northern Bolivia
ranges.Crypturellus brevirostris: disjunctly in humid forest of northwestern Brazil and probably adjacent far eastern Colombia; and the Guianas and northeastern Amazonian Brazil (Amapá)
ranges.Crypturellus casiquiare: far eastern Colombia and adjacent southern Venezuela
ranges.Crypturellus undulatus: varied lowland forest and moist woodland types of cis-Andean South America from eastern Colombia and Ecuador east through the Guianas to Piauí and Bahia (northeastern Brazil); in south to Chaco Province (north-central Argentina) and São Paulo Province (southeastern Brazil)
ranges.Crypturellus noctivagus: lowlands of eastern Brazil from Piauí to Rio Grande do Sul
ranges.Crypturellus transfasciatus: tropical forest of western Ecuador to northwestern Peru
ranges.Crypturellus cinnamomeus: deciduous forest and edge in lowlands and hills from northern Sinaloa to southern Oaxaca in west, and in the east from Nuevo León southward through the Yucatan Peninsula and then south on the Pacific slope to northwestern Costa Rica
ranges.Crypturellus atrocapillus: lowlands of southeastern Peru from Ayacucho south and Acre (western Brazil) to central Bolivia
ranges.Crypturellus strigulosus: tropical southern Amazonian Brazil, adjacent eastern Peru and northwestern Bolivia
ranges.Crypturellus duidae: tropical forest of east-central Colombia to southern Venezuela
ranges.Crypturellus erythropus: woodland and scrub of lowlands and hills of northern South America north of the Amazon River, from north-central Colombia through northern Venezuela to Amapá (northern Brazil)
ranges.Crypturellus kerriae: humid foothills of far southeastern Panama and northwestern Colombia
ranges.Crypturellus boucardi: lowland and hill forest of Caribbean slope from southern Mexico from central Veracruz eastward to southeastern Costa Rica
ranges.Anhima cornuta: lowlands of Venezuela to northern Bolivia and Amazonian Brazil
ranges.Chauna torquata: wet lowlands of southeastern Peru to northern Argentina and southern Brazil
ranges.Anseranas semipalmata: south-central New Guinea, northern and eastern Australia (Kimberley region eastward to northern Queensland, southward to southeastern South Australia)
ranges.Thalassornis leuconotus: local in wetlands of sub-Saharan Africa and Madagascar
ranges.Dendrocygna arborea: Bahamas, Greater Antilles, and northern Lesser Antilles
ranges.Dendrocygna autumnalis: southern USA (where expanding range) to northern Argentina (mainly east of Andes)
ranges.Dendrocygna eytoni: northern and eastern Australia (Pilbara and Kimberley regions eastward to northern Queensland, southward to northern Victoria)
ranges.Dendrocygna bicolor: eastern Africa, Madagascar, and southern Asia; disjunctly southern USA to Argentina
ranges.Dendrocygna guttata: southern Philippines and Sulawesi to New Guinea, Bismarck Archipelago, and northern Australia (Tiwi Islands off Northern Territory, and north-eastern Queensland)
ranges.Dendrocygna viduata: Africa, Madagascar, and Comoros; disjunctly Costa Rica to Brazil
ranges.Dendrocygna javanica: Indian subcontinent to southeastern Asia and Greater Sundas
ranges.Dendrocygna arcuata: Sumatra and Philippines to Australia, New Guinea, and New Britain (southeastern Bismarck Archipelago)
ranges.Nettapus auritus: sub-Saharan Africa (except southwestern Africa) and Madagascar
ranges.Nettapus pulchellus: eastern Lesser Sundas, southern Moluccas, southern New Guinea, and tropical northern and eastern Australia (Kimberley region of Western Australia to central-eastern Queensland)
ranges.Nettapus coromandelianus: lowlands of India, southern Asia, Indonesia, New Guinea, and coastal northeastern Australia
ranges.Heteronetta atricapilla: lowlands of central Chile to Paraguay and southward to central Argentina
ranges.Nomonyx dominicus: northeastern Mexico and Caribbean southward to South America; west of the Andes to western Ecuador, and east of the Andes to northern Argentina and Brazil
ranges.Oxyura leucocephala: patchily distributed Mediterranean basin to central Asia
ranges.Oxyura australis: southwestern and southeastern Australia, including Tasmania
ranges.Oxyura maccoa: local in highlands of eastern and southern Africa
ranges.Oxyura vittata: breeds southern Argentina and Chile; winters northward to southern Brazil and Paraguay
ranges.Oxyura jamaicensis:
interior northwestern North America (southwestern Canada to Mexico), West Indies, and western South America (Andes of central Colombia to southern Argentina and southern Chile)
central and eastern Andes of Colombia
ranges.Coscoroba coscoroba: southern Brazil to Paraguay, Uruguay, Tierra del Fuego, and Falkland Islands
ranges.Cereopsis novaehollandiae: islands off southern Australia; winters to adjacent coast
ranges.Cygnus melancoryphus: southern South America from Tierra del Fuego and Falkland Islands northward to central Chile, Uruguay, and far southern Brazil (Rio Grande do Sul); in winter northward to São Paulo (southeastern Brazil)
ranges.Cygnus olor: west-central to east-central Palearctic region from central Europe to southeastern China; partially migratory southward; introduced widely including to western and southwestern Europe, Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu), southwestern Australia, and eastern North America
ranges.Cygnus atratus: Australia including Tasmania but not tropical north; New Zealand, where formerly occurred but was eradicated, later was reintroduced and also self-colonized
ranges.Cygnus columbianus: high Arctic breeder of Holarctic; winters to southern Palearctic and southern USA
ranges.Cygnus cygnus: breeds Palearctic; winters to central Asia and southeastern China
ranges.Cygnus buccinator: breeds North America from western and central Alaska eastward through east-central Canada and southward through western and central USA; some southward movement in winter; early extirpations and subsequent reintroductions cloud distributional knowledge
ranges.Branta bernicla: arctic tundra, coastal meadows, and small islands in lakes and rivers in coastal Alaska, northern Canada, Arctic Canadian islands, northern Greenland, Svalbard, and northern Siberia, Russia; winters in southern Alaska southward to the coast of northwestern Mexico and Baja California, and along the eastern coast of Canada and the US, in the British Isles, Iceland, the western coast of Europe, southern Russia, northeastern China, Japan, and the Korean Peninsula
ranges.Branta ruficollis: breeds low Arctic tundra of Yamal, Gydan, and Taymyr peninsulas (northwestern Siberia); winters to western and southern Black Sea and southern Caspian Sea; prone to vagrancy elsewhere in Eurasia
ranges.Branta sandvicensis: upland lava flows, grassy areas, and wetlands of Hawaiian Islands (Hawaii); reintroduced to Kaua‘i and Maui
ranges.Branta canadensis: breeds most of North America; winters mostly USA
ranges.Branta leucopsis: breeds high Arctic eastern Greenland, Svalbard (north of Norway), Novaya Zemlya, and nearby Kolguyev and Vaygach islands (northwestern Russia); winters to coastal northern British Isles, southern Scandinavia, and northwestern Europe
ranges.Branta hutchinsii: breeds high Arctic of North America; winters western and central USA, less often north-central Japan (Honshu)
ranges.Anser indicus: breeds alpine lakes in central Asia; winters to India and Myanmar
ranges.Anser canagicus: breeds in northeastern Siberia and western Alaska; winters mainly in Alaska, from the Aleutians to the Alaska Peninsula
ranges.Anser rossii: breeds tundra of Arctic north-central Canada; winters to western and central USA and central Mexico
ranges.Anser caerulescens: arctic tundra near wetlands in the islands of northern Canada and northwestern Greenland southward to the Arctic coast of Canada and Alaska, coastal Hudson Bay, Wrangel Island, and far northeastern Siberia; winters locally in western US, in central US mainly along the Mississippi River basin, and in the Atlantic coast of the US and southward to northern Mexico, southward in the highlands of central Mexico to northern Jalisco and Guanajuato, and along the Gulf of Mexico coast southward to Veracruz, less often north-central Japan (Honshu)
ranges.Anser anser: open freshwater wetlands, swamps, lakes, coastal lagoons, and open fields from Iceland, northern Europe, and northern Scandinavia eastward across eastern Europe, Türkiye, the Caucasus, Kazakhstan, and southern Russia to northeastern China and southeastern Russia; winters in western and southern Europe, northernmost Africa, and Türkiye eastward to eastern China and Taiwan
ranges.Anser cygnoides: breeds central Asia and Mongolia to southeastern Siberia; winters to southeastern China
ranges.Anser erythropus: breeds Arctic Eurasia; winters to southern Europe, India, and China
ranges.Anser albifrons: Holarctic, breeding in southwestern Greenland, northern Russia to Chukotskiy Peninsula, and northern Alaska to west of Hudson Bay; winters to southern Europe, Middle East, eastern China, Korean Peninsula, Japan (Honshu), and southwestern and southeastern USA and northern Mexico
ranges.Anser serrirostris: breeds Arctic lakes, pools, and rivers from northern Scandinavia (including Svalbard) eastward across northern Siberia to northeastern Russia; winters in central and eastern Europe, eastern China, and Japan
ranges.Anser brachyrhynchus: breeds Greenland, Iceland, and Spitsbergen; winters northwestern Europe
ranges.Anser fabalis: taiga rivers, lakes, and pools from northern Scandinavia eastward across the Ural Mountains and northerrn Siberia to northern Mongolia, northeastern China, and southeastern Russia; winters mostly in northern and central Europe, central Asia, eastern China, and Japan
ranges.Merganetta armata: Andean streams of western South America from Venezuela to southern Chile and Argentina in Tierra del Fuego
ranges.Callonetta leucophrys: southern Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
ranges.Cairina moschata: lowland wetlands from northern Mexico southward, west of the Andes, to southwestern Ecuador and, east of the Andes, to northeastern Argentina and Brazil; domestic varieties introduced almost worldwide
ranges.Aix galericulata: breeds wooded ponds, swamps, and streams of northeastern Asia from southeastern Siberia, eastern China, Korean Peninsula, Japan (Hokkaido to central Ryukyu Islands), and Taiwan; winters to southeastern China and northern southeastern Asia; introduced in Western Europe, and escapes frequent in USA
ranges.Aix sponsa: breeds mainly inland waters of southern Canada from southern British Colombia and Montana to southern California in the west, and eastern Saskatchewan eastward to Nova Scotia and southward to east-central Texas and southern Florida and Cuba; mainly resident in west of range; in east winters mainly from east-central USA southward to central Mexico and the Bahamas
ranges.Neochen jubata: Orinoco and Amazon basins to northwestern Argentina
ranges.Chloephaga melanoptera: Andes of southern Peru to northwestern Argentina and central Chile
ranges.Chloephaga poliocephala: southern Argentina and southern Chile to Tierra del Fuego
ranges.Chloephaga rubidiceps: resident Falkland Islands; breeds southernmost Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego; migrates northward to southern Buenos Aires Province, Argentina
ranges.Chloephaga hybrida: coastal southern Argentina and Chile to Tierra del Fuego and Falkland Islands
ranges.Chloephaga picta: breeds southern Chile, southern Argentina, and Falkland Islands; winters northward to central Chile and northern Argentina
ranges.Radjah radjah: Moluccas, New Guinea and satellite islands, and northern and eastern Australia
ranges.Alopochen aegyptiaca: Nile Valley of Egypt and Sudan, and sub-Saharan Africa; introduced to western and central Europe, and southeastern USA
ranges.Alopochen mauritiana: formerly Mauritius; extinct, likely since late 1600s
ranges.Alopochen kervazoi: formerly Réunion; extinct, likely since late 1600s
ranges.Tadorna tadorna: breeds western Europe to east-central Asia; winters to northern Africa through southern and eastern Asia
ranges.Tadorna cristata: formerly Siberia and Korea; probably extinct, last reported 1916
ranges.Tadorna ferruginea: breeds Iberian Peninsula and Mediterranean northern Africa eastward through southern Russia to eastern China, and in the south through Türkiye to Tibetan Plateau including Ladakh; winters to Ethiopia, southern India, and eastern Asia; introduced in central Europe and the Canary Islands, and appears frequently elsewhere
ranges.Tadorna variegata: North, South, Stewart, and satellite islands (New Zealand)
ranges.Tadorna tadornoides: southwestern and southeastern Australia, including Tasmania and satellite islands
ranges.Clangula hyemalis: breeds coastal Greenland (except northern), Iceland, northern Fennoscandia, northern Russia to Chukotka Peninsula, Alaska and northern Canada; winters mostly in coastal bays of northwestern Europe, northern Japan (Hokkaido and northern Honshu), and Korean Peninsula, and Aleutians to southwestern Canada
ranges.Polysticta stelleri: breeds northwestern and northeastern Siberia from Yamal Peninsula to Chukotka, and Arctic Coastal Plain, northern Alaska; winters to Kamchatka Peninsula, Commander and Kuril islands (southeastern Russia), and Aleutians; also northernmost Norway and the Kola Peninsula, and Baltic, White, and Barents seas
ranges.Camptorhynchus labradorius: formerly coastal northeastern North America; extinct, last reported 1875
ranges.Somateria fischeri: breeds north-central and northeastern Siberia from Lena Delta to Chukotka, and western and northern Alaska in Yukon Delta and Arctic Coastal Plain; winters polynyas (ice-free seas) between St. Lawrence and St. Matthew (northern Bering Sea)
ranges.Somateria spectabilis: breeds coastal northern and central Greenland, Svalbard (north of Norway), Russia from east of the White Sea to Chukotka (northeastern Russia); Arctic Coastal Plain of Alaska, northern slope of Canada and associated Arctic islands; winters to Kamchatka (southeastern Russia) and Aleutians, Newfoundland (southeastern Canada), southern Greenland, Iceland, and northern Norway
ranges.Somateria mollissima: breeds central and southern coastal Greenland, Iceland, Faroe Islands, northwestern Europe to Chukotka Peninsula (northeastern Russia), Alaska through Arctic Canada to Massachusetts (northeastern USA); winters to France, Kamchatka (southeastern Russia), Aleutians, and Long Island (New York)
ranges.Histrionicus histrionicus: breeds eastern Siberia and northern Japan (Hokkaido to central Honshu), Alaska southward to Oregon and Wyoming, eastern Canada (southeastern Baffin Island southward to the Gulf of St. Lawrence), Greenland, and Iceland; winters coastally from Siberia to Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu) and Korean Peninsula, from Alaska to central California, to the northeastern USA, southern Greenland, and Iceland
ranges.Melanitta nigra: breeds southeastern Greenland, Iceland, Scotland, and northern and western Scandinavia to Olenyok River (north-central Siberia); winters to Baltic and North sea coasts, and eastern Atlantic coast to northwestern Africa
ranges.Melanitta americana: breeds Yana River to Kamchatka (eastern Siberia), Alaska eastward to northwestern Yukon; eastern Northwest Territories and southwestern Nunavut to Newfoundland (central to eastern Canada); winters to southern Japan; Aleutians, eastern North Pacific coast to central California; western North Atlantic coast from Newfoundland to northern Florida
ranges.Melanitta perspicillata: breeds mainland Alaska through subarctic Canada eastward to Labrador; winters eastern Aleutians to Baja California, and Prince Edward Island to North Carolina, less often northeastern Japan (Hokkaido)
ranges.Melanitta fusca: breeds northern Europe from Norway to Yenisey River (central Siberia) and northeastern Kazakhstan, also Türkiye and Georgia; winters to Baltic Sea, Denmark, and eastern coast of Britain
ranges.Melanitta deglandi: breeds subarctic western Alaska to eastern shore of James Bay (east-central Canada); winters Aleutians to central California (eastern North Pacific coast); and Gulf of St. Lawrence to New Jersey, less often off northeastern Japan
ranges.Melanitta stejnegeri: breeds Yenisey Basin to Kamchatka (central and eastern Siberia), northeastern Kazakhstan, and northern and western Mongolia; winters to Kuril and Commander islands (southeastern Russia), coasts of Japan (Hokkaido to southern Honshu), and eastern Korean Peninsula (northeastern Pacific)
ranges.Bucephala albeola: breeds subarctic west-central Alaska and Canada eastward to eastern Quebec and (locally) northwestern and north-central USA; winters to central Mexico and northern Florida, less often northern Japan
ranges.Bucephala islandica: breeds central Alaska southward to Oregon (formerly to northern California) and Wyoming; also in eastern Canada and Iceland; winters from southern Alaska to California and Wyoming, from the Maritime Provinces (Canada) southward to northeastern USA, and Iceland
ranges.Bucephala clangula: breeds subarctic from Scotland and Scandinavia to Sakhalin and Kamchatka (southeastern Russia), in south through northern Kazakhstan, northern Mongolia, and Heilongjiang (northeastern China); western Alaskan mainland to Labrador and New Brunswick, in south through northern tier of contiguous USA; winters to southern Europe, eastern China, and middle tier of USA
ranges.Mergellus albellus: breeds northern Eurasia; winters to North Africa, India, and eastern China
ranges.Lophodytes cucullatus: breeds southeastern Alaska to northwestern USA, southern Manitoba to Nova Scotia (central and southeastern Canada) southward to eastern Texas and northern Florida; winters to southern California, southern Texas, and southern Florida
ranges.Mergus serrator: breeds southern Greenland, Iceland, northern British Isles, and Scandinavia to Sakhalin and Kamchatka peninsulas, and Kuril and Commander islands (southeastern Russia), in south through northern Kazakhstan and northeastern China; western Alaska mainland through mainland Canada from Arctic to northern Great Lakes and eastward to Nova Scotia; winters to coasts of southern Europe, Black and Caspian seas, Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu), Korean Peninsula, and eastern China, and to west-central Mexico, Gulf Coast, and Florida
ranges.Mergus squamatus: breeds eastern Siberia, Korean Peninsula, and northeastern China; winters southern Japan to southern China
ranges.Mergus octosetaceus: forest rivers, now mostly in a few sites in southeastern Brazil, at least formerly also in Paraguay and Misiones (northeastern Argentina); rare
ranges.Mergus australis: formerly Auckland Islands; extinct, last reported 1902
ranges.Mergus merganser: breeds Iceland, northern and central Europe, subarctic Russia through northeastern Kazakhstan, and northeastern Afghanistan through Tibet and western China, northern Mongolia to Kamchatka, Hokkaido (northern Japan) and northeastern China; southwestern Alaska mainland through subarctic Canada to Newfoundland, southward through western USA and to northern Great Lakes; winters to central Europe and eastern China, and to southern California and Maryland
ranges.Sarkidiornis melanotos: tropical Africa and Madagascar; disjunctly India to southern China
ranges.Sarkidiornis sylvicola: tropical South America (east of the Andes) to northern Argentina
ranges.Hymenolaimus malacorhynchos: central and southern North Island and western South Island (New Zealand)
ranges.Chenonetta jubata: Australia including Tasmania (but not western deserts or Cape York Peninsula)
ranges.Pteronetta hartlaubii: local in forest streams of equatorial western and central Africa
ranges.Marmaronetta angustirostris: Canary Islands and Mediterranean basin to far southwestern China
ranges.Asarcornis scutulata: northeastern India to southeastern Asia (rare), Sumatra, and (formerly) Java
ranges.Rhodonessa caryophyllacea: formerly India and Myanmar; probably extinct, last reported 1935
ranges.Netta rufina: breeds from Europe (Iberian Peninsula northward to southern Denmark and Poland) eastward to central Asia (northwestern China and western Mongolia); somewhat local in Europe, more widespread to east; resident in southwestern Europe; elsewhere, winters from eastern Mediterranean eastward to northern and central India, south-central China, northern Myanmar, and southern Japan
ranges.Netta erythrophthalma: eastern and southern Africa; disjunctly tropical South America, mainly eastern Brazil
ranges.Netta peposaca: lowlands of southeastern Brazil to southern Argentina and Chile
ranges.Aythya nyroca: breeds discontinuously through southern Palearctic, from Spain through northeastern China; winters to India, southeastern Asia, eastern China, and southern Japan (central Honshu to Kyushu)
ranges.Aythya innotata: Lac Alaotra and Lac Matsaborimena (north-central and northwestern Madagascar, respectively); thought extinct until rediscovered at Lac Matsaborimena in 2006
ranges.Aythya baeri: breeds northeastern Asia; winters to southern Japan (southern Honshu to Kyushu), southern China and southeastern Asia (now rare everywhere)
ranges.Aythya australis: Australia including Tasmania, Vanuatu (Banks Islands to Tanna), eastern Lesser Sundas, and southern New Guinea
ranges.Aythya ferina: Palearctic, breeding British Isles and southern Scandinavia eastward through east-central Russia, in south from Iberian Peninsula and Türkiye eastward through northeastern China and northern Japan (northern Hokkaido, rare); winters to tropical Africa and India eastward to Japan (Honshu to Ryukyu Islands) and southward to the northern Philippines
ranges.Aythya valisineria: breeds North America from northern Alaska and western Canada southward through northern California, southern Colorado, and Minnesota (USA); winters to central Mexico, less often to central Japan
ranges.Aythya collaris: breeds Alaska to southern USA; winters to Panama and southern Lesser Antilles, less often to central Japan
ranges.Aythya americana: breeds Alaska to southern USA; winters to Guatemala and Greater Antilles
ranges.Aythya fuligula: breeds northern Palearctic from Iceland eastward to Kamchatka, southward to central Europe, Mongolia, and northern Japan (northern Hokkaido, rare); winters to northern Africa and southern and southeastern Asia including Philippines
ranges.Aythya affinis: breeds North America from northern Alaska and western Canada southward through northern California, southern Colorado, and Minnesota (USA); winters to Hawaiian Islands, the Caribbean, and northern South America
ranges.Aythya marila: breeds subarctic from Iceland and Scandinavia to Kamchatka and the Commander Islands (southeastern Russia), and Alaska eastward to northern Quebec (eastern Canada); winters to coasts of northwestern and east-central Europe, Black and Caspian seas, eastern China, Korean Peninsula, Japan (Hokkaido to Ryukyu Islands), and Taiwan, and central California, Great Lakes, and North Carolina (southwestern to east-central USA)
ranges.Lophonetta specularioides: Andes of northwestern Peru to southern South America through Tierra del Fuego and Falkland Islands
ranges.Speculanas specularis: breeds mainly forested regions of southern Chile and Argentina; some winter northward to central Chile and Argentina, or to non-freezing waterbodies at low elevations
ranges.Amazonetta brasiliensis: smaller lowland wetlands, mostly in wooded areas, of cis-Andean South America from east-central Colombia east throughout Brazil and southward to northwestern and east-central Argentina
ranges.Tachyeres pteneres: southern South America, from southern Chile (north to Llanquihue) southward to Tierra del Fuego
ranges.Tachyeres patachonicus: southern Chile (northward to Maule) and southern Argentina (northward to Neuquén and southern Buenos Aires); scarce Falkland Islands
ranges.Sibirionetta formosa: breeds in northern and eastern Siberia; winters Japan (Honshu to Kyushu), Korean Peninsula, and eastern China
ranges.Spatula querquedula: breeds Palearctic (except north); winters to central Africa through Indonesia
ranges.Spatula hottentota: local in sub-Saharan Africa and Madagascar
ranges.Spatula puna: Andes of Peru to northwestern Argentina and northern Chile
ranges.Spatula versicolor: southern Bolivia, Paraguay, and southern Brazil southward to southern Chile and southern Argentina and Falkland Islands
ranges.Spatula platalea: southern Peru eastward to southern Brazil and southward to Tierra del Fuego and Falkland Islands
ranges.Spatula discors: breeds North America (except Arctic and western Alaska), mostly in central prairie regions; winters northern Mexico to Caribbean and coastal northern South America
ranges.Spatula cyanoptera: western North America from British Colombia southward to northwestern Mexico; disjunctly western and southern South America
ranges.Spatula clypeata: breeds Holarctic (except Arctic); winters through eastern Africa, southern, southeastern, and eastern Asia, Philippines, the Caribbean, and Central America
ranges.Spatula rhynchotis: southern Australia including Tasmania, and North and South islands (New Zealand)
ranges.Mareca falcata: breeds Mongolia, eastern Siberia, northeastern China, and northern Japan (northern Hokkaido); winters sparingly from northern plains of India to southern and eastern China, South Korea, and Japan (Honshu to northern Ryukyu Islands)
ranges.Mareca strepera: breeds temperate Holarctic; winters to northern Africa, southern Asia, and southern Mexico; formerly Line Islands, where extinct since c. 1874
ranges.Mareca marecula: formerly Amsterdam and St. Paul islands; extinct, last reported 1793

ranges.Lophura edwardsi: lowlands of central Vietnam (perhaps extinct in wild, but persists in captivity)

ranges.Lophura ignita: lowland and hill forest (including logged forest) of Bangka (east of south Sumatra) and Borneo

ranges.Galloperdix bicalcarata: humid forest of southern Sri Lanka
ranges.Polyplectron malacense: southern Myanmar to southern Thailand and Malayan Peninsula
ranges.Polyplectron katsumatae: very local in forest of southern Hainan (southeastern China)
ranges.Polyplectron bicalcaratum: northeastern India and Bhutan eastward to far southern China, southward to the base of the Thai-Malay Peninsula, central Laos, and central Vietnam
ranges.Polyplectron chalcurum: hill and lower montane forest (including logged forest) of Sumatra
ranges.Bambusicola fytchii: foothill to montane tall grassland, open scrub forest, thickets, and bamboo, from northeastern India and eastern Bangladesh eastward through south-central China (Sichuan and Yunnan), Myanmar, and southward to northwestern Thailand, northern Laos, and northern Vietnam
ranges.Bambusicola thoracicus: varied habitats and elevations of central and southeastern China; introduced Honshu to Kyushu (central to southern Japan)
ranges.Bambusicola sonorivox: bamboo thickets and bushy areas in hills of Taiwan; introduced northern Kyushu (southern Japan)
ranges.Gallus varius: Java eastward to Alor (central Lesser Sundas); introduced Cocos (Keeling) Islands (northeastern Indian Ocean)
ranges.Gallus gallus: native range fragmented in lowland to lower montane open woodland, moist forest, and mangroves, from northeastern India eastward across Himalayan foothills to southern China (including Hainan), and southward through eastern India and southeastern Asia to Vietnam, the Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, Java, and Bali. Feral junglefowl widespread throughout native range, and likely introduced to Philippines, Sulawesi, and parts of the Lesser Sundas (Indonesia). Feral populations widely introduced away from native range, including Micronesia, Melanesia, and Polynesia; domesticated stock released in open warm habitats globally, including North America, South Africa, New Zealand, and many tropical islands.
ranges.Peliperdix lathami: lowland and hill forest including gallery forest, from eastern Sierra Leone eastward to southern South Sudan, Uganda, and northwestern Tanzania, and southward to Cabinda (northwestern Angola)
ranges.Campocolinus coqui: grassland and woodland of lowlands and hills in Sahel, East Africa, and south-central to southern Africa, from southern Mauritania eastward to southern Nigeria and southward to Angola; central Ethiopia through eastern Africa southward to eastern and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, thence west to northern Namibia and southeastward to KwaZulu-Natal
ranges.Campocolinus schlegelii: Cameroon, southern Chad, northern Central African Republic, far southwestern Sudan and northwestern South Sudan
ranges.Campocolinus albogularis: scrub and disturbed savanna of lowlands from Senegal eastward to northern Cameroon; disjunctly, local in eastern Angola, northwestern Zambia, and southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
ranges.Scleroptila streptophora: southwestern Cameroon; western Uganda to western Kenya and northwestern Tanzania
ranges.Scleroptila levaillantii: moist and ungrazed grassland of hills and mountains of eastern and southern Africa, from eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to central Kenya and southward to northwestern Tanzania; disjunctly in southern Tanzania southward to southern Malawi and west to west-central Angola; northeastern South Africa southward to the Cape
ranges.Scleroptila finschi: patchily distributed in Congo, southwestern Democratic Republic of the Congo and central Angola
ranges.Scleroptila psilolaema: montane moorlands of central and southern Ethiopia
ranges.Scleroptila elgonensis: montane moorlands of eastern Uganda to central Kenya
ranges.Scleroptila afra: grassland of Lesotho and west-central South Africa
ranges.Scleroptila gutturalis: grassland and scrub to mountains of northeastern and southern Africa, from Eritrea and northern Somalia through South Sudan to northern Uganda and northern Kenya; disjunctly from coastal central Angola and northern Namibia eastward to northeastern South Africa
ranges.Scleroptila whytei: southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to northern Zambia and northern Malawi
ranges.Scleroptila shelleyi: southern Uganda and southwestern Kenya to northeastern South Africa

ranges.Ortygornis pondicerianus: grassland and scrub of lowlands and hills from southeastern Iran northward in Indus Valley to northern sub-Himalayan Pakistan and eastward along base of Himalayas to southeastern Nepal and southward to far western Bangladesh, south throughout Peninsular India to northern Sri Lanka; introduced to Hawaiian Islands (Oahu and Hawaii)
ranges.Francolinus pintadeanus: dry scrub from Manipur and Mizoram (southeastern India) and Myanmar (except north) east through southern Yunnan and northeast to Zhejiang (eastern China); in south to northern Malayan Peninsula and through southeastern Asia; Hainan

ranges.Francolinus francolinus: scrub and wet grassland of lowlands and hills of Caucasus of Georgia and Azerbaijan, and northwestern Iran, from southern Türkiye, Cyprus, and Iraq to Israel and western Jordan, eastward through southern Iran and Afghanistan to northern sub-Himalayan Pakistan and eastward to western Assam, and southward to central Manipur, northern Bangladesh, and northern Odisha; introduced to Cyprus, United Arab Emirates, Kutch (Gujarat, western India), Guam, and Hawaii (all main islands)
ranges.Tetraogallus tibetanus: alpine and upper montane open slopes, alpine pastures, and stony ridges above tree-line, from the eastern Pamirs in Tajikistan and eastern Kyrgyzstan southeastward across northwestern India, Tibet, to the eastern Himalayas to south-central China, and northward to west-central China (Qinghai, Sichuan, and western Gansu)
ranges.Tetraogallus altaicus: open alpine habitats to snowline of far northeastern Kazakhstan, southwestern Siberia, northern Xinjiang, and western and central Mongolia
ranges.Tetraogallus caucasicus: rocky high-montane Caucasus of southwestern Russia, northern Georgia, and northern Azerbaijan
ranges.Tetraogallus caspius: rocky high-montane central Türkiye through southern Georgia and Azerbaijan to northeastern and south-central Iran
ranges.Tetraogallus himalayensis: alpine and subalpine rocky terrain and alpine meadow, from Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and eastern Kazakhstan eastward to western and west-central China, and southward to northern and eastern Afghanistan, northern Pakistan, northwestern India, and western Nepal; introduced to Ruby Mountains, Nevada (USA)
ranges.Ammoperdix griseogularis: dry foothills and plateaus of southeastern Türkiye, northern Syria, and (locally) northern Saudi Arabia to southern Armenia, Uzbekistan, southeastern Turkmenistan, southern Tajikistan southward through Iran and Afghanistan (except northeastern), to sub-Himalayan Pakistan
ranges.Ammoperdix heyi: rocky areas with scattered vegetation in desert and semi-desert from southernmost Syria and northern Jordan southward to the Sinai Peninsula and across the Arabian Peninsula to southern Oman and southern Yemen, and along the eastern coast of Egypt to northeastern Sudan
ranges.Synoicus chinensis: lowland to lower montane dense and swampy grassland, grassy scrub, and unkempt cultivation, from northern, southern, and eastern India, and Sri Lanka, Andaman and Nicobar islands, eastward to southern China and Taiwan, and southward through southeastern Asia, Philippines, and Indonesia, to New Guinea, the Bismarck Archipelago, and northern and eastern Australia; nomadic wandering post-breeding; introduced to Guam (in western Pacific) and Réunion (Mascarenes)
ranges.Synoicus monorthonyx: alpine grassland of Snow Mountains (west-central New Guinea)
ranges.Synoicus ypsilophorus: wet grassland of lowlands and locally high mountains of central and eastern Lesser Sundas, northern and eastern New Guinea, and Australia (except south-central), including Tasmania; introduced to North Island (New Zealand)
ranges.Coturnix japonica: breeds in eastern Asia, from northern Mongolia northeastward through Baikal region to Vitim region of east-central Russia, eastward to Sakhalin, and southward to Japan (to central Honshu), Korean Peninsula, and northeastern China (eastern Shandong); also (presumably) in Bhutan and Myanmar; winters southward from central Japan and central China westward through northwestern Thailand and northern Myanmar to Bhutan and Assam, with small numbers as far northward as Buryatia and Ussuriland (Russia) in mild winters; introduced to Hawaiian Islands (Kauai and Hawaii, where now rare)
ranges.Coturnix coturnix: breeds Europe (including Atlantic islands) eastward to Mongolia and Bhutan, and southward to southern Africa, the Comoros, and Madagascar; northern populations migrate to Sahel zone; introduced Mauritius and Réunion (Mascarenes)
ranges.Coturnix coromandelica: Pakistan to Myanmar and western Thailand
ranges.Coturnix delegorguei: patchy in grassland and lightly wooded savanna in sub-Saharan Africa from Chad, Cameroon and São Tomé (Gulf of Guinea) eastward to Ethiopia, thence southward to Angola and northern Namibia to eastern South Africa (avoiding rainforest and arid southwestern Africa), plus southwestern Arabian Peninsula and western Madagascar; movements associated with rain and nomadic, westward to Ivory Coast
ranges.Coturnix novaezelandiae: formerly New Zealand; extinct, last reported 1875
ranges.Coturnix pectoralis: Australia including Tasmania, but not far north (Kimberley region of northern Northern Territory, and Cape York Peninsula)

ranges.Alectoris melanocephala: arid regions of southern Arabian Peninsula to Yemen and Oman
ranges.Alectoris rufa: varied drier open habitats in lowlands to hills from Iberian Peninsula and France through northern Italy and Corsica; introduced to British Isles and from Azores southeast through Canary Islands
ranges.Alectoris chukar: open dry often rocky areas of lowlands to high mountains from eastern Greece and southeastern Bulgaria to far southwestern Russia and Türkiye southward through Sinai (eastern Egypt) and northwestern Saudi Arabia, eastward through Iran, and northward through Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan, and Mongolia eastward to Liaoning (northeastern China); in south through Afghanistan, Pakistan, and western Himalayas through eastern Nepal; introduced to United Arab Emirates, South Island (New Zealand), Hawaiian Islands (all main islands), and southwestern Canada and western USA

ranges.Alectoris philbyi: rocky desert of southwestern Saudi Arabia and northern Yemen
ranges.Alectoris magna: arid montane northern Qinghai and west-central Gansu (north-central China)
ranges.Ophrysia superciliosa: formerly west-central Himalayas; probably extinct, last reported 1876
ranges.Perdicula asiatica: far northern sub-Himalayan India southward to Gujarat and eastern Rajasthan, eastward south of Himalayas to southern West Bengal, southward through Peninsular India, and southeastern Sri Lanka
ranges.Perdicula argoondah: lowland semidesert of western Gujarat northeast to southern Haryana and southeastward to central Madhya Pradesh, southward through central Tamil Nadu
ranges.Perdicula erythrorhyncha: grassland and scrub of hills and mountains, in Western Ghats of India from southern Maharashtra southward to southern Tamil Nadu; disjunctly northeastern Peninsular India, where poorly known
ranges.Perdicula manipurensis: tall grassland of lowlands to hills, historically from northeastern West Bengal through Assam and Manipur; few recent records, sight only
ranges.Pternistis hartlaubi: rocky hill country of southwestern Angola to central Namibia
ranges.Pternistis nobilis: montane forest of eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, southwestern Uganda, and Rwanda
ranges.Pternistis camerunensis: western Cameroon (southeastern and northeastern slopes of Mount Cameroon)
ranges.Pternistis castaneicollis: hill and montane forest of north-central Ethiopia to northwestern Somalia, southward to southern Ethiopia, and far northern Kenya
ranges.Pternistis erckelii: northeastern Sudan and highlands of northern Eritrea and northwestern Ethiopia; introduced to Hawaiian Islands (all main islands)
ranges.Pternistis ochropectus: montane forest of Forêt du Day (Djibouti)
ranges.Pternistis swierstrai: montane forest of western Angola (Cuanza Sul to Huila)
ranges.Pternistis ahantensis: discontinuous in lowlands of Senegambia to southwestern Nigeria
ranges.Pternistis griseostriatus: locally in escarpment of western Angola

ranges.Pternistis adspersus: southern Angola to Namibia, Botswana, southwestern Zambia, and western Zimbabwe
ranges.Pternistis natalensis: Zambia and Mozambique to Cape Province
ranges.Pternistis hildebrandti: Kenya to Tanzania, southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, northeastern Zambia, and southern Malawi
ranges.Pternistis bicalcaratus: varied open habitats in lowlands and hills of western Morocco and disjunctly from southern Mauritania eastward to northeastern Cameroon and southward to southern Cameroon

ranges.Tachybaptus novaehollandiae: Java, Sangihe, and Talaud islands (north of Sulawesi), Timor (eastern Lesser Sundas), New Guinea, southeastern Bismarck Archipelago, Australia, New Zealand, Vanuatu, New Caledonia, and Rennell (southern Solomon Islands)

ranges.Tachybaptus ruficollis: Europe (except north) to central, southern, and eastern Asia and Philippines; Africa and Malagasy region; Java, Sulawesi region, Lesser Sundas, Moluccas, northern New Guinea, Bismarck Archipelago, and Solomon Archipelago

ranges.Tauraco rossae: riparian forest and woodland of central Africa

ranges.Limnodromus scolopaceus: breeds wet meadows from Lena River through northeastern Siberia, St. Lawrence Island (Bering Sea; rare), western Alaska and northern Northwest Territories (north-central Canada); winters inland from Japan (Honshu to Ryukyu Islands) and the southern US through Mexico, along the Pacific coast from the Pacific Northwest southward to northwestern Costa Rica, and along the Atlantic and Gulf coasts from the mid-Atlantic southward to the Yucatan Peninsula
ranges.Limnodromus griseus: breeds north temperate bogs in tundra and muskeg from Gulf of Alaska and inland south-central Alaska, southwestern Yukon, and montane northwestern British Columbia (northwestern Canada); north-central Alberta to western Manitoba (central Canada); southwestern Hudson and James bays to western Labrador (east-central Canada); winters coastal mudflats and mangroves from northern California to northern Peru and Galapagos, and North Carolina to northeastern Brazil
ranges.Lymnocryptes minimus: breeds taiga wetlands from Scandinavia and northeastern Poland to east-central Siberia; winters inland wetlands from Faroe and British islands, western and southern Europe, Mediterranean, tropical Africa, Middle East, and southern and eastern Asia
ranges.Scolopax minor: breeds temperate forest and edge from southwestern Alberta eastward to Maritime Provinces (south-central to southeastern Canada) and southward to southeastern Texas and northern Florida (southeastern USA); winters in southeastern USA
ranges.Scolopax rusticola: breeds locally in moist woodland and bogs from British Isles and Scandinavia southward to northern Iberian Peninsula and Azores to Canary Islands, eastward to southeastern Russia southward to central Japan (Honshu and Izu Islands), and disjunctly in the Caucasus and Himalayas; winters southward to northern Africa and eastward to central and southern Japan (to Ryukyu Islands) and Taiwan
ranges.Scolopax mira: Amami-Oshima, Tokunoshima, Okinawa, Tokashiki-Shima (Ryukyu Islands, southern Japan)
ranges.Scolopax bukidnonensis: cloudforest and clearings, from lowlands to mountains of Calayan and Babuyan (Babuyan Islands, northernmost Philippines), and montane Luzon and Mindanao (northern and southern Philippines, respectively)
ranges.Scolopax saturata: mountains of Sumatra and western Java
ranges.Coenocorypha iredalei: formerly South and Stewart islands (subfossils only); historically known only from islands off Stewart Island (New Zealand); apparently extinct, last recorded 1964
ranges.Coenocorypha barrierensis: formerly North Island (subfossils only); historically known only from Little Barrier Island (off northeastern North Island), New Zealand; extinct, last recorded 1870
ranges.Coenocorypha aucklandica: Antipodes Islands (southeast of Stewart Island) and Auckland and Campbell islands (south of South Island; New Zealand)
ranges.Coenocorypha pusilla: Rangatira, Mangere, Little Mangere, and Rabbit islands, and Star Keys, Chatham Islands; originally found throughout Chatham Islands
ranges.Coenocorypha huegeli: Snares Islands (Northeast, Broughton, and Alert Stack), south of New Zealand; introduced to Codfish Island, off Stewart Island
ranges.Gallinago imperialis: elfin forest montane bogs from Ecuador to Peru (old records Colombia)
ranges.Gallinago undulata: wet grassland of northern and southeastern South America from eastern Colombia through French Guiana, and disjunctly southeastern Peru and Bolivia (where very rare) through Bahia (northeastern Brazil) and southward through Paraguay and Rio Grande do Sul (southeastern Brazil)
ranges.Gallinago stricklandii: bogs of temperate central and southern Chile and southern Argentina to Cape Horn and Isla de los Estados (east of Tierra del Fuego)
ranges.Gallinago jamesoni: montane bogs from west-central Venezuela to north-central Bolivia
ranges.Gallinago nemoricola: breeds alpine meadows of western Himalayas from Himachal Pradesh to eastern India and south-central China; winters to lower-elevation wetlands and woodlands, rarely to Indian Peninsula and northern southeastern Asia
ranges.Gallinago solitaria: breeds montane wetlands of central and eastern Palearctic from Altai and Tian Shan mountains of south-central Russia, northeastern Kazakhstan, northwestern Xinjiang, and northern Mongolia eastward to Kamchatka and northeastern China; winters montane eastern Kazakhstan to eastern Afghanistan, Himalayas, northern southeastern Asia, west-central to southeastern China, Korean Peninsula, Sakhalin and Amurland (southeastern Russia), and Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu)
ranges.Gallinago media: breeds meadows from northern Scandinavia and eastern Poland eastward to Yenisei River (western Siberia); winters wet grassland of tropical and subtropical sub-Saharan Africa
ranges.Gallinago megala: breeds wooded wetlands of south-central Siberia and northeastern Kazakhstan eastward to Amurland (southeastern Russia); winters wetland edge from east-central China, Taiwan, Philippines, and Malayan Peninsula eastward through New Guinea, Melanesia, and Micronesia
ranges.Gallinago stenura: breeds low Arctic tundra to temperate montane meadows from northwestern Siberia and northeastern Kazakhstan eastward to Sea of Okhotsk (eastern Siberia); winters inland wetlands from southern Arabian Peninsula eastward through southern Asia to Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan) and southward to Taiwan and Greater Sundas
ranges.Gallinago hardwickii: breeds meadows and fields of eastern Amurland and southern Sakhalin (southeastern Russia) southward through Kyushu (Japan); winters freshwater wetlands of eastern Australia including Tasmania
ranges.Gallinago macrodactyla: marshes of eastern and central massif of Madagascar
ranges.Gallinago nigripennis: subtropical to tropical wetlands of Africa from Eritrea southward through eastern Africa and Angola southward through South Africa
ranges.Gallinago delicata: breeds central Aleutians to eastern Canada and northern tier of continental USA; winters south of breeding range to northern South America
ranges.Gallinago gallinago: breeds low Arctic to temperate wetlands of Palearctic from Iceland to British Isles, Scandinavia, France, and Azores eastward through northern Russia to central Chukchi Peninsula, Kamchatka, Sea of Okhotsk, and Commander Islands (southeastern Russia); in south to northern Kazakhstan, eastern Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Afghanistan, Kashmir (northwestern Himalayas), northern Mongolia, and northeastern China; winters temperate to tropical wetlands mainly north of Equator from British Isles to southern Europe, Atlantic islands, northern Africa, west-central to east-central Africa, Middle East, central to southern Asia, eastern China, Taiwan, Korean Peninsula, central and southern Japan, Philippines, and Greater Sundas
ranges.Gallinago nobilis: montane wet grassland far western Venezuela to far northern Peru
ranges.Gallinago andina: montane wet grassland of western South America from Peru to northern Chile and northwestern Argentina
ranges.Gallinago paraguaiae: wetlands from central Colombia and Trinidad through the Guianas southward to northern Argentina and Uruguay
ranges.Gallinago magellanica: breeds from central Chile and central Argentina southward to Tierra del Fuego and Falkland Islands; southernmost populations are migratory, nonbreeding distribution unclear but reaches Uruguay
ranges.Xenus cinereus: breeds low Arctic tundra and taiga from Finland and Ukraine eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula and southward to western Amurland (eastern Russia); winters mainly coastal mudflats and estuaries from eastern Africa eastward to Taiwan and northern Australia
ranges.Actitis hypoleucos: breeds inland waterbody margins from British Isles and Scandinavia eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula (northeastern Russia), in south from Iberian Peninsula across Caucasus to Kashmir (northwestern Himalayas), northeastern China, and Japan (Hokkaido to northern Honshu); winters from southwestern Europe and Africa eastward to southern Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Melanesia, and Micronesia
ranges.Actitis macularius: breeds inland waterbody margins from Aleutians and Alaska mainland except North Slope eastward through Canada (except far northern) to Newfoundland, and southward to southwestern and east-central USA; winters southern USA and Caribbean southward to northern Chile and Argentina
ranges.Phalaropus tricolor: breeds inland marshes of western and central Canada to west-central USA; molt migration to hypersaline lakes of western Canada and USA; winters mainly saline montane lakes from Peru to Argentina; also western coast of South America from Ecuador southward, and Argentina to Tierra del Fuego
ranges.Phalaropus fulicarius: breeds mostly high Arctic marshy tundra from southern Greenland and Iceland (local) eastward across Siberia to northern Alaska and northern Canada including southern tier of Arctic Canadian islands; winters off coasts from California to southern Chile, Atlantic USA to northern Florida, and off western Africa
ranges.Phalaropus lobatus: breeds mostly low Arctic tundra from southern Greenland and Iceland eastward to Kamchatka, Kuril, and Commander islands, and Aleutians through Canada; winters off coasts of Indian Ocean from Arabian Sea eastward through Indonesian Archipelago and in Pacific to New Guinea and Bismarck Archipelago and western Mexico to Peru and Galapagos
ranges.Tringa ochropus: breeds taiga wetlands from Scandinavia and Germany eastward to Sakha Republic (northeastern Siberia), southward through central Asia and northeastern China; winters wetlands from British Isles southward through Africa and eastward to central and southern Japan through Philippines
ranges.Tringa solitaria: breeds subarctic to temperate zone taiga muskeg from Alaska mainland (except far north) to southwestern Canada, eastward to Hudson and James bays and north of Great Lakes to eastern Quebec (at least); winters inland subtropical to tropical small wetlands from west-central Mexico, southern Texas, and the Caribbean to central Peru and north-central Argentina
ranges.Tringa incana: breeds montane tundra from Chukotka (northeastern Siberia) through Alaskan mainland (except far north) to northwestern Canada; winters mainly rocky Pacific coasts from eastern Australasia, Melanesia, Micronesia, Polynesia, isolated eastern Pacific islands, and southwestern Canada to Ecuador
ranges.Tringa brevipes: breeds montane tundra of Krasnoyarsk (west-central Siberia) and Yana River eastward to Kamchatka (eastern Siberia); winters muddy to sandy Pacific coasts from southern Japan (southern Ryukyu Islands), Malayan Peninsula eastward through Micronesia and western Polynesia and southward to northern Australia
ranges.Tringa stagnatilis: breeds freshwater marshes from eastern Poland and Baltic states eastward through southern Russia and northern Kazakhstan to Amurland and northeastern China; winters wetlands from Africa eastward through southern Asia to southern Japan (Ryukyu Islands) and Mariana Islands, and southward to Australia
ranges.Tringa glareola: breeds wooded wetlands from Scotland and Scandinavia eastward through inland northern Russia to eastern Siberia and northeastern China, in south through northern Mongolia to Commander Islands (southeastern Russia); winters small wetlands from Africa eastward to southern Japan (Ryukyu Islands) and southward to Australia
ranges.Tringa totanus: breeds subarctic to temperate coastal and inland marshes and meadows from Iceland to northern Scandinavia and southward to Iberian Peninsula and coastal Tunisia, in north from Baltics, southwestern Russia, Kazakhstan, and northern Mongolia eastward to Amurland (southeastern Russia), southward through northern Middle East, most of central Asia, Himalayas, Tibetan Plateau, and eastward to northeastern China and far northern Japan (eastern Hokkaido); winters temperate to tropical inland and coastal wetlands from southern British Isles, Africa (except southern), Middle East, southern Asia to eastern China, Philippines, Taiwan, and Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), and Indonesian Archipelago
ranges.Tringa flavipes: breeds subarctic tundra to forest from Alaska mainland eastward to James Bay and probably central Quebec (east-central Canada); winters southern USA throughout Caribbean southward to Tierra del Fuego
ranges.Tringa erythropus: breeds wooded tundra from Scandinavia eastward through inland Russia to Chukotskiy Peninsula (northeastern Siberia); winters wetlands from southern British Isles and tropical Africa eastward through southern Asia and southern Japan (Ryukyu Islands) to southeastern China and Taiwan
ranges.Tringa nebularia: breeds taiga wetlands from Scotland and Scandinavia eastward through temperate Russia to far eastern Russia; winters from southern Europe and Africa eastward through southern Asia to central Japan and southward to Australia and western Micronesia
ranges.Tringa melanoleuca: breeds taiga muskeg from southern Alaska eastward through southern tier of Canadian provinces to eastern Labrador (eastern Canada); winters wetlands of southern USA and throughout Caribbean southward to Tierra del Fuego
ranges.Tringa guttifer: breeds coastal larch forest of western and southern coastal Sea of Okhotsk, Tatar Strait (west of Sakhalin), and Sakhalin (eastern Siberia); winters coastal mudflats and saltpans of southeastern Bangladesh, southern Myanmar, Thai-Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, and southwestern Borneo
ranges.Tringa semipalmata: breeds in coastal saltmarshes of coastal Newfoundland (southeastern Canada) to Florida southward to Tamaulipas (northeastern Mexico), also Bahamas, Greater Antilles, and scattered islands elsewhere in Caribbean including Los Roques (north of Venezuela); rarely migrates inland; winters coastally from New Jersey through Caribbean southward to northeastern Brazil
ranges.Tringa inornata: breeds in prairies wetlands of inland central Alberta eastward to southwestern Manitoba (south-central Canada), southward to northeastern California and northern Nebraska; frequently migrates inland; winters coastally northern California to central Chile
ranges.Prosobonia cancellata: formerly Kiritimati (Christmas) Island (Line Islands); extinct, not reported since discovery in 1778
ranges.Prosobonia parvirostris: remote uninhabited atolls of the Tuamotu Archipelago (French Polynesia), with known breeding on islands of Tenararo, Morane, Reitoru, Tahanea, and Raraka
ranges.Prosobonia leucoptera: formerly Tahiti (Windward Society Islands); extinct, not reported since discovery in 1773
ranges.Prosobonia ellisi: formerly Moorea (Windward Society Islands); extinct, not reported since discovery in 1777
ranges.Arenaria melanocephala: breeds coastal and inland waterbodies of western Alaska; winters rocky coastal southeastern Alaska to southern Baja California, Gulf of California, and Sonora (northwestern Mexico)
ranges.Arenaria interpres: breeds high and low Arctic tundra of coastal Holarctic; winters temperate to tropical coasts worldwide, including oceanic islands
ranges.Calidris canutus: breeds patchily in high Arctic (mainly) tundra of Holarctic from northwestern and eastern Greenland, north-central Siberia, islands north of north-central and northeastern Siberia, and northern Chukotskiy Peninsula (northeastern Siberia); winters coasts worldwide from temperate zone to tropics; in Indian Ocean mainly western Australia, and in Pacific in New Zealand but rare on other remote islands
ranges.Calidris virgata: breeds montane tundra of Alaska mainland (except far northern) and Yukon (northwestern Canada); winters rocky coasts from southeastern Alaska to Tierra del Fuego
ranges.Calidris tenuirostris: breeds montane tundra of northeastern Siberia from Yakutsk eastward to Anadyr Peninsula; winters coasts from northeastern Arabian Peninsula eastward to Taiwan, Philippines, and Australia
ranges.Calidris pugnax: breeds tundra and steppe of northwestern Europe from Scandinavia southward to northern Ukraine and eastward to far eastern Siberia; winters from central Europe southward through Africa, eastward through southern Asia to central Japan southward to Philippines
ranges.Calidris acuminata: breeds low Arctic tundra from Lena to Kolyma rivers (northeastern Siberia); winters from Wallacea eastward through Australasia; prone to extreme vagrancy
ranges.Calidris falcinellus: breeds patchily in low Arctic to subarctic tundra bogs of northern Palearctic from Scandinavia to Kanin Peninsula (northwestern Russia); Taimyr Peninsula (northwestern Siberia) and Lena to Kolyma rivers (northeastern Siberia); winters Paleotropical coasts from eastern Africa, Red Sea, and Persian Gulf through southeastern Asia, Indonesian Archipelago, southern New Guinea, and Australia (except south and Tasmania)
ranges.Calidris ferruginea: breeds drier tundra from Yamal Peninsula to northwestern Chukotskiy Peninsula (northwestern to northeastern Siberia), including New Siberian Islands; winters southern Europe and Africa eastward through southern Asia to Taiwan and Philippines and southward to Melanesia; prone to extreme vagrancy
ranges.Calidris himantopus: breeds tundra to taiga edge of North Slope of Alaska eastward to north-central Canada; winters Mexico and throughout the Caribbean; in Central America mainly along Pacific coast; coastal South America to Peru and northern Brazil, and in pampas of north-central Argentina
ranges.Calidris pygmaea: breeds coastal tundra of eastern Chukotskiy Peninsula to northern Kamchatka (northeastern Russia); winters coastal mudflats from Taiwan and east-central China to Bangladesh; mainly Thailand, Myanmar, and Bangladesh; rare and local
ranges.Calidris ruficollis: breeds coastal tundra of Taymyr Peninsula eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula and northern Kamchatka Peninsula (north-central to north-eastern Siberia); winters coastal northeastern India and Sri Lanka eastward to southern Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Philippines, Australasia, and Melanesia
ranges.Calidris temminckii: breeds tundra of Scandinavia eastward through northern Russia to Chukotskiy Peninsula (northeastern Russia), including New Siberian Islands; winters southeastern Europe southward to central Africa and eastward to central and southern Japan and Taiwan
ranges.Calidris subminuta: breeds subarctic to temperate bogs of disjunctly in Chukotskiy Peninsula, northern Kuril and Commander islands (eastern Russia) and (perhaps) northern Mongolia; winters eastern India and Sri Lanka eastward through southern Asia to southern Japan (Ryukyu Islands) and southward to southeastern Australia
ranges.Calidris subruficollis: breeds high Arctic dry coastal tundra from Wrangel Island (northeastern Siberia) eastward through Alaskan North Slope to northeastern Canada, including Arctic islands from Banks to Devon; migrates to grassland of southeastern Brazil and Uruguay to central Argentina; prone to extreme vagrancy worldwide
ranges.Calidris alba: breeds high Arctic tundra wetlands of Holarctic from northwestern and southeastern Greenland, Svalbard (north of Norway), north Taymyr Peninsula and Severnaya Zemlya (to the north), Lena Delta, and New Siberian Islands (north-central Siberia), Alaskan North Slope (rare), Canadian Arctic islands from Banks to Ellesmere and south to Southampton; winters sandy coastal beaches worldwide from temperate to tropical zone, in Old World from the British Isles and Atlantic islands through Africa, Malagasy region, Middle East, southern Asia through Indonesian Archipelago to Australia, Melanesia, Philippines, and southern and central Japan (but rare New Guinea and New Zealand); in New World, southwestern and southeastern Canada and Caribbean southward to Tierra del Fuego, and including remote islands of eastern Polynesia
ranges.Calidris alpina: breeds low (locally high) Arctic to temperate wet tundra of Holarctic, from southwestern and northeastern Greenland, Iceland, Faroe Islands, northern British Isles, Scandinavia, Baltic region east through northern Russia including Novaya Zemlya (north of northwestern Siberia) and New Siberian Islands (north of east-central Russia), through Chukotskiy Peninsula, western Kamchatka, northern Kurile and northern Sakhalin islands (eastern Russia); Aleutians, western and northern Alaska and northwestern Canada, and north-central Canada north and west of Hudson Bay; winters coastal and inland wetlands from temperate to tropical zones mainly north of Equator, from British Isles, western Europe, Mediterranean, northern and north-central Africa, Middle East, and northern plains of India to northern Vietnam and eastern China, Taiwan, Korean Peninsula, and Japan (Honshu to Ryukyu Islands); southwestern Canada and New England to west-central Mexico and Yucatan Peninsula
ranges.Calidris maritima: breeds montane tundra from Greenland and Iceland eastward through Arctic Europe and Russia to Taymyr Peninsula (north-central Siberia), also Banks to southern Ellesmere and Baffin islands (north-central Canada); winters rocky North Atlantic coasts from Iceland and Faroe Islands to western Europe, and Labrador and Gulf of St. Lawrence (southeastern Canada) southward to North Carolina
ranges.Calidris ptilocnemis: breeds coastal low Arctic to subarctic tundra of far northern Pacific from eastern Chukotskiy Peninsula to (disjunctly) southern Kamchatka, Commander and (perhaps) northern Kuril islands (eastern Russia), Aleutian and Bering Sea islands, western Alaska from Seward Peninsula to Gulf of Alaska islands; winters rocky subarctic to temperate coasts to Hokkaido (northern Japan) and central California
ranges.Calidris bairdii: breeds high Arctic dry tundra from Wrangel Island to eastern Chukotskiy Peninsula (northeastern Siberia) through northern and central Alaska, northern Canada including Arctic islands from Banks to Ellesmere and Baffin islands, and northwestern Greenland; winters in mountains and coastally from southern Peru through Chile and southern Argentina
ranges.Calidris melanotos: breeds wet tundra from Yamal Peninsula eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula (northwestern to eastern Siberia), including New Siberian and Wrangel islands, also western and northern Alaska eastward through northeastern Canada, including Arctic islands; winters wet grassland and wetland edge mainly to Peru, Bolivia, and southern Brazil southward to Tierra del Fuego; prone to extreme vagrancy
ranges.Calidris pusilla: breeds tundra from eastern Chukotskiy Peninsula (northeastern Siberia) through northern Alaska and eastward in northern Canada to northern Labrador, including southern Canadian Arctic islands from Banks to Baffin; winters coasts from Isthmus of Tehuantepec and Yucatan Peninsula (southwestern Mexico) and Caribbean to far northern Chile and northeastern Brazil
ranges.Calidris mauri: breeds Chukotskiy Peninsula and Anadyr (northeastern Siberia; few), St. Lawrence Island (Bering Sea), and western and northern Alaska mainland; winters coastal Washington to Peru and Galapagos, southeastern Canada to Caribbean, and inland central Mexico to northern Costa Rica
ranges.Calidris minuta: breeds drier tundra from northern Scandinavia eastward through northern Russia to New Siberian Islands (east-central Siberia); winters mudflats and marshes from southern Europe and Africa eastward to southern Asia and southern Japan
ranges.Calidris minutilla: breeds tundra and taiga wetlands from eastern Aleutian Is through Alaska and Canada eastward to Labrador and Nova Scotia; winters mudflats and wetlands from southeastern USA, Caribbean, and Mexico southward to northern South America
ranges.Calidris fuscicollis: breeds wet tundra from North Slope of Alaska eastward in coastal northern Canada to northwestern Hudson Bay, and Banks to Devon and Baffin islands (northeastern Canada); winters to wetlands of southern Chile, southeastern Brazil, northwestern to southeastern Argentina, and Falkland Islands
ranges.Ortyxelos meiffrenii: discontinuously distributed Sahel of sub-Saharan Africa
ranges.Turnix tanki: grassland, stubble, and scrub of lowland to hills from southern and eastern Pakistan (where rare) through sub-Himalayan region to southern India, east through Qinghai and to Amurland (southeastern Russia), southward through Nicobar Islands and northern Malaysia and to southern Vietnam; some withdrawal to south of northern populations in winter
ranges.Turnix maculosus: grassland and scrub of lowlands to montane Sulawesi and Lesser Sundas eastward to southern and eastern New Guinea, northern and eastern Australia, and (at least formerly) New Britain (southeastern Bismarck Archipelago)
ranges.Turnix suscitator: grassland, crops, and scrub of lowlands to mountains from northeastern and southeastern Pakistan east through sub-Himalayan zone of India southward to Sri Lanka and east through southwestern to eastern China, Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), Taiwan, Philippines, through southeastern Asia and Indonesia through Sulawesi and the northern Lesser Sundas eastward to Alor
ranges.Turnix ocellatus: grassland, brush, and crops of lowlands and mountains of Luzon (northern Philippines)
ranges.Turnix sylvaticus: dry scrub, savanna, and burnt areas in lowlands to mountains from far southern Iberian Peninsula (at least formerly) and northern Morocco; most of sub-Saharan Africa; southwestern Arabian Peninsula; northern and southeastern Pakistan east through eastern China, southward through India and east through Vietnam; Philippines (where rare), and disjunctly Java and Bali
ranges.Turnix velox: grassland and woodland in Australia (except Tasmania)
ranges.Turnix pyrrhothorax: savanna and scrub of northern, central and eastern Australia (Kimberley region, northern Western Australia, eastward to eastern South Australia)
ranges.Turnix nanus: Ghana to Kenya, Uganda, and southeastern Cape Province
ranges.Turnix hottentottus: mountains of South Africa (southwestern Cape Province to Port Elizabeth)
ranges.Turnix castanotus: northwestern Australia (Kimberley region, northern Northern Territory) and offshore islands
ranges.Turnix olivii: northeastern Australia (Cape York Peninsula, northern Queensland); possibly extinct, last verified record 1924
ranges.Turnix varius: wooded scrub and tussocky areas in lowlands and hills of southwestern Australia including Houtman Abrolhos Islands (off southwest); and southeastern and eastern Australia including Tasmania and islands in Bass Strait
ranges.Turnix novaecaledoniae: formerly New Caledonia; probably extinct, not certainly reported since 1889
ranges.Turnix melanogaster: coastal eastern Australia (southeastern Queensland, and formerly northern New South Wales)
ranges.Turnix nigricollis: Madagascar; introduced (?) Mauritius, Réunion, and Glorieuses
ranges.Dromas ardeola: coasts of Indian Ocean, breeding on shores of northwestern Indian Ocean, Persian Gulf, and Red Sea; non-breeders regularly range southward to Kenya, Tanzania, and Madagascar, and eastward to western India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Chagos, and Andaman Islands (possibly breeds in the last four sites); also small numbers to northeastern South Africa, and to southwestern Thailand
ranges.Smutsornis africanus: tropical to subtropical stony plains of eastern and southern Africa, disjunctly in Djibouti, Ethiopia, and northern Somalia; southern Kenya, and Tanzania; and southwestern Angola to southwestern Zimbabwe and through South Africa
ranges.Rhinoptilus cinctus: tropical bushland and open woodland from Ethiopia and Somalia through eastern Africa to northern South Africa and west to northern Namibia
ranges.Rhinoptilus bitorquatus: tropical scrub jungle of Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh (east-central India); extremely rare, with very few recent records
ranges.Cursorius temminckii: tropical to subtropical savanna of sub-Saharan Africa from southern Mauritania eastward to Eritrea and western Somalia, southward to northern South Africa
ranges.Cursorius coromandelicus: dry stony plains of north-central Pakistan, sub-Himalayan India, far southern Nepal, and far northern Sri Lanka
ranges.Cursorius cursor: subtropical to tropical desert of western Paleotropics, from eastern Canary Islands and Cabo Verde, northwestern Africa, Middle East from southeastern Türkiye to Socotra, Iran, and western Turkmenistan to far northwestern India
ranges.Cursorius somalensis: semidesert in lowlands to hills from Eritrea and eastern Ethiopia throughout Somalia, southward to far southeastern South Sudan and east through southeastern Kenya; some intratropical migration
ranges.Cursorius rufus: semidesert of southwestern Angola to Namibia, Botswana, and South Africa
ranges.Glareola ocularis: breeds rocky coastal and river islets of northwestern and eastern Madagascar; winters coasts and estuaries of eastern Africa from southern Somalia to northern Mozambique
ranges.Glareola nuchalis: rocky rivers of tropical Africa from southeastern Gambia and Guinea-Bissau, disjunctly eastward to South Sudan and Ethiopia, eastward to western Kenya and southward to northern Namibia and Mozambique
ranges.Glareola isabella: breeds northern Australia (Kimberley region, northern Western Australia, eastward to inland eastern Australia and southward to northern Victoria); winters south-eastern Indonesia to southern New Guinea
ranges.Glareola lactea: eastern Afghanistan and Pakistan to India and Indochina
ranges.Glareola cinerea: rivers of Mali to Cameroon, western Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northwestern Angola
ranges.Glareola maldivarum: breeds patchily in grassland near water from western India and Sri Lanka eastward to southeastern Siberia and Japan (central Honshu to Ryukyu Islands), southward to Philippines; winters grassy fields of Indian Ocean islands from Seychelles to Maldives, and Indian Peninsula and Sri Lanka eastward through northern Australia and the Mariana Islands and Bismarck Archipelago
ranges.Glareola nordmanni: breeds saline steppe near water from central Ukraine and southwestern Russia eastward to eastern Kazakhstan; winters in grassland near water of eastern Namibia, Botswana, and northern South Africa
ranges.Glareola pratincola: patchily southern temperate to tropical grassland near water, from southern Europe and northern Africa through central Asia eastward to western Xinjiang (northwestern China) and northwestern India; also sub-Saharan river systems except far south
ranges.Stercorarius parasiticus: breeds mostly low Arctic tundra from Greenland, Iceland, and Scotland eastward to northeastern Siberia and Kamchatka, Aleutian and Bering Sea islands, through Alaska to east-central Arctic Canada (except northern high Arctic islands); winters to coastal waters of Africa, Persian Gulf, western India and Sri Lanka, eastward to Japan and Australasia, and southern South America
ranges.Stercorarius longicaudus: breeds Holarctic high and low Arctic tundra, locally in subarctic, from northwestern and southeastern Greenland, Arctic northern Scandinavia to northeastern Siberia and Kamchatka (eastern Russia); Arctic, western, and southern Alaska through Arctic Canada to Ellesmere and Baffin islands; in winter highly pelagic and mostly occurs southerly, to offshore subantarctic and subtropical waters off Africa, Madagascar, southern Australia, Peru, Chile, and east-central Argentina
ranges.Stercorarius pomarinus: breeds high Arctic tundra, mainly northwestern to northeastern Russia (including many high Arctic islands), northern and southwestern Alaska, eastward through Arctic Canada to Baffin Island (northeastern Canada); winters to temperate to tropical coasts and offshore waters worldwide
ranges.Stercorarius skua: breeds Iceland, Faroe Islands, Ireland, Scotland, Norway including Svalbard, and northwestern Russia to Novaya Zemlya; winters North Atlantic Ocean offshore waters to central Gulf Stream of New England to North Carolina, northeastern Brazil, North Sea to Iberian Peninsula, western Mediterranean, Atlantic islands, and western Africa
ranges.Stercorarius maccormicki: breeds coastal Antarctica, especially Ross Sea; also South Shetland and South Orkney islands (off Antarctic Peninsula); winters to northern offshore waters and North Indian Ocean: mostly clockwise to Japanese and Korean waters and Gulf Stream of eastern USA, then southwestern Canada to northern Baja California and northwestern Africa
ranges.Stercorarius chilensis: breeds coasts of southern Chile and southern Argentina; ranges north to coasts of southern Peru and central Brazil
ranges.Stercorarius antarcticus: southern oceans and coasts from coastal southern Argentina, Falkland Islands, Tristan da Cunha group (south-central South Atlantic), subantarctic and Antarctic islands from Cape Horn to New Zealand region
ranges.Cerorhinca monocerata: breeds North Pacific islands from Sakhalin and Kuril Islands, Hokkaido and northern Honshu (northern Japan), Aleutians, southern Alaska to southern California; winters coastal waters to southern Japan and Korean Peninsula and northern Baja California
ranges.Fratercula cirrhata: breeds North Pacific coasts and islands from northern Chukotka and Sea of Okhotsk through Kuril and Commander islands (eastern Russia), off southeastern Hokkaido (northern Japan), eastward through Bering Sea Islands and Aleutians and southern Alaska southward to central California; winters offshore in North Pacific Ocean, and nearshore to southern Japan and southern California
