ranges.Phaethon rubricauda: breeds tropical and subtropical islands of South Indian and Pacific oceans; pelagic when not breeding, to waters off southeastern Africa, southwestern and eastern Indonesia, southern Japan, Taiwan, and eastern Australia
ranges.Phaethon lepturus: widespread breeder, all tropical oceans (except eastern Pacific and northeastern Atlantic); pelagic when non-breeding, to waters off eastern Africa, western and southern Sri Lanka, Indonesian Archipelago, and New Guinea waters, east-central Australia, and Gulf Stream north to North Carolina
ranges.Gavia stellata: breeds across the northern Holarctic region; winters coastally in the north Pacific Ocean from the Kamchatka Peninsula and Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu) to the Yellow Sea, and from southern Alaska to northwestern Mexico; and in the northern Atlantic Ocean from the Maritime Provinces (Canada) to the southeastern USA, from Scandinavia south to the Mediterranean, and the Black and Caspian seas
ranges.Gavia immer: breeds in southern Greenland, Iceland, and northern North America southward to northern tier of US states; winters from Iceland and Scandinavia southward to the Iberian Peninsula and from southern Alaska and the Maritime Provinces (Canada) southward to northern Mexico
ranges.Gavia adamsii: breeds Arctic northwestern Russia from Novaya Zemlya eastward to Chukotka Peninsula, through northern Alaska and northern Canada to Nunavut (east-central Canada); winters to northern Norway, Japan (northern Honshu), Korean Peninsula, and coastal British Columbia (southwestern Canada); prone to extreme vagrancy
ranges.Gavia pacifica: breeds coastal eastern Siberia and northern North America eastward through northern Canada to Baffin Island and James Bay (eastern Canada); winters to Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu) and southern Baja California
ranges.Gavia arctica: breeds Arctic to temperate northern and central Eurasia and far western Alaska; non-breeders to coastal southern European and western Asian seas, to Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu) and Korean Peninsula
ranges.Aptenodytes patagonicus: breeds on beaches of subantarctic islands, in Tierra del Fuego, Falkland Islands, South Georgia, South Sandwich Islands, Prince Edward, Crozet, Kerguelen, and Heard islands, and Macquarie Island (southeast of Australia); disperses widely at sea mostly around Antarctic Convergence
ranges.Aptenodytes forsteri: breeds in scattered colonies on Antarctic continent edge and up to 200 km from open sea; ranges Antarctic seas to edge of ice pack and beyond, juveniles dispersing most widely
ranges.Pygoscelis adeliae: breeds circumpolarly along coastline of Antarctica and associated islands; winters near edge of ice pack
ranges.Pygoscelis antarcticus: breeds on Antarctic Peninsula and associated islands, including Balleny Island (eastern Antarctica); winters mostly south of Antarctic Convergence, to southern South America and subantarctic islands
ranges.Pygoscelis papua: mainly subantarctic islands, locally Antarctic islands
ranges.Eudyptula minor: southern Australia and North, South, Stewart and Chatham islands (east of South Island; New Zealand)
ranges.Spheniscus demersus: breeds coastal southern Namibia and southern South Africa; ranges to central Namibia and southeastern Africa
ranges.Spheniscus magellanicus: breeds coastal central Chile and central Argentina to Cape Horn and Falkland Islands; winters to southeastern Brazil
ranges.Spheniscus humboldti: Humboldt Current region of coastal northern Peru to central Chile
ranges.Megadyptes antipodes: very local on coasts of South (where now very rare), Stewart and satellites, Auckland, and Campbell islands (New Zealand)
ranges.Eudyptes chrysolophus: subantarctic islands in South Atlantic Ocean and southern Indian Ocean
ranges.Eudyptes schlegeli: breeds on coastal slopes of Macquarie and nearby Bishop and Clerk islands (southeast of Australia); winters mostly near colonies, with juveniles ranging farther
ranges.Eudyptes sclateri: breeds among rocks of Bounty and Antipodes islands (New Zealand); winters to waters of eastern South Island
ranges.Eudyptes pachyrhynchus: breeds inland in forests of southwestern South Island, western and southern Stewart Island, and satellites (New Zealand); winters to seas south of Australia
ranges.Eudyptes robustus: breeds coastal forest of Snares Islands; disperses westward to waters off southeastern Australia, and northward off New Zealand
ranges.Eudyptes moseleyi: breeds among coastal rocks and tussocks of Tristan da Cunha group and Gough (South Atlantic), and St. Paul and Amsterdam islands (South Indian Ocean)
ranges.Eudyptes chrysocome: breeds far southern Chilean islands of Magallanes Province to Cape Horn Archipelago and Falkland Islands; winters northward along Patagonian coast
ranges.Eudyptes filholi: breeds coastally on Prince Edward, Crozet, Kerguelen, Heard (southern Indian Ocean), Macquarie (southeast of Australia), and Auckland, Campbell, and Antipodes islands (New Zealand)
ranges.Phoebastria irrorata: breeds Española (Galapagos) and Isla La Plata off Ecuador; ranges to coastal waters of Ecuador and northern Peru
ranges.Phoebastria albatrus: breeds Torishima (Izu Islands) and Senkaku Islands; ranges through North Pacific
ranges.Phoebastria nigripes: breeds Senkaku, Izu, and Ogasawara (Bonin) islands (southern Japan) and Hawaiian Islands (most of population; Northwestern to islets in main group); ranges North Pacific from Bering Sea to Tropic of Cancer
ranges.Phoebastria immutabilis: breeds Ogasawara (Bonin) Islands (rare; formerly also Torishima, southern Japan), northwestern Hawaiian Islands (most of population, Northwestern eastward to Oahu), and Guadalupe and Revillagigedo islands (western Mexico); ranges North Pacific
ranges.Diomedea epomophora: breeds Enderby Island (Auckland Islands) and Campbell Islands (New Zealand); ranges all south temperate and subantarctic oceans
ranges.Diomedea sanfordi: breeds mostly Sisters and Forty Fours (Chatham Islands), also Otago Peninsula of southeastern South Island (New Zealand); ranges all southern temperate and subantarctic oceans, mostly Pacific
ranges.Diomedea dabbenena: breeds Inaccessible and Gough islands (Tristan da Cunha group); ranges subtropical and temperate southern Atlantic Ocean
ranges.Diomedea antipodensis: breeds Chatham, Antipodes, Auckland, and Campbell islands (east and south of South Island, New Zealand); non-breeders to Tasman Sea (off southeastern Australia) and southeastern Pacific
ranges.Diomedea exulans: breeds high-latitude islands of South Georgia, Prince Edward, Crozet, Heard, Kerguelen, and Macquarie islands; ranges all southern oceans
ranges.Diomedea amsterdamensis: breeds Amsterdam Island (French subantarctic islands); ranges mainly south Indian Ocean
ranges.Phoebetria palpebrata: breeds circumpolar subantarctic islands; ranges through subantarctic and Antarctic oceans
ranges.Phoebetria fusca: breeds temperate zone islands of South Atlantic and south Indian oceans; ranges through temperate zone of those oceans
ranges.Thalassarche chlororhynchos: breeds Tristan da Cunha and Gough islands; ranges southern oceans
ranges.Thalassarche carteri: breeds on southern Indian Ocean islands; ranges mainly southern Indian Ocean between Tropic of Capricorn and Subtropical Convergence
ranges.Thalassarche chrysostoma: breeds circumpolar high southern latitudes; ranges southern oceans mostly south of South Polar Front
ranges.Thalassarche melanophris: breeds islands of south Chile, Falkland, South Georgia, and South Sandwich (southeast of South Georgia), Crozet, Heard, Kerguelen (South Indian Ocean), Macquarie (far southeast of Australia), Antipodes, Snares, and Campbell groups (southeast and south of South Island, New Zealand), and Campbell and Jeanette Marie islands (Campbell Islands, south of South Island, New Zealand); non-breeders are widespread all southern oceans from north of Antarctic Convergence to Tropic of Capricorn
ranges.Thalassarche bulleri: breeds islets of northwestern North Island (rare), Chatham Islands (east of South Island), west of Stewart Island, and Snares (south of South Island, New Zealand); non-breeders to Australian waters and western coast of South America
ranges.Thalassarche cauta: breeds Tasmania and Auckland Islands (south of South Island, New Zealand); non-breeders to southern Indian and Pacific oceans
ranges.Thalassarche salvini: breeds mostly Bounty Islands, a few in Snares and Crozet islands; ranges to temperate and subtropical waters off southeastern Australia, western South America, and southern Africa
ranges.Thalassarche eremita: breeds Pyramid Rock (Chatham Islands); ranges in Humboldt and Magellanic currents off southern Peru and Chile
ranges.Oceanites oceanicus: breeds islets in southern Chilean fjords and Cape Horn Archipelago; many islands, coasts, and inland sites in Antarctica; Falkland, South Georgia, Crozet, Heard, Kerguelen (southwestern to southeastern Indian Ocean), and Macquarie islands (far southeast of Australia); non-breeders throughout world oceans except tropical and North Pacific
ranges.Oceanites pincoyae: known only from waters near Chiloé Island (Reloncavi Sound and the Chacao Channel), Chile
ranges.Oceanites gracilis: breeds Chungunga Island (Coquimbo, central Chile) at least; probably also Galapagos; non-breeders range Humboldt Current from Ecuador to central Chile and Galapagos
ranges.Nesofregetta fuliginosa: now breeds on predator-free islands mainly in Line, Marquesas, Gambier, Austral, and Easter island groups, formerly much more widespread, including westward to New Caledonia, Vanuatu, Fiji, and Samoa
ranges.Garrodia nereis: breeds circumpolar subantarctic islands in Falkland Islands, South Georgia, Gough (Atlantic), Crozet and Kerguelen (Indian Ocean), Macquarie (few; Australia), Chatham, Antipodes, and Auckland (New Zealand) islands; ranges mainly between Antarctic and Subantarctic convergences, northward to southern Tasman Sea and about 35°S
ranges.Pelagodroma marina: breeds Salvage (northwest of Canary Islands), Canary Islands, and Cabo Verde, Tristan da Cunha group including Gough (south-central Atlantic Ocean), southern Australian islets, and New Zealand region; non-breeders range to subtropical waters in North and South Atlantic, northwestern and tropical Indian Ocean to Seychelles, and southeastern Pacific Ocean
ranges.Fregetta lineata: breeds New Caledonia; ranges from the Coral Sea (just off eastern Australia) eastward to Samoa and the Marquesas Islands
ranges.Fregetta grallaria: breeds tropical and subtropical southern ocean islands: south-central Indian Ocean islands, Lord Howe Island (far east of Australia), Kermadec Islands (northeast of North Island, New Zealand), Rapa (Austral Islands, eastern Polynesia), San Felix and San Ambrosio (Easter Island, southeastern Polynesia), and Juan Fernandez Islands (far west of central Chile); non-breeders range tropical and subtropical southern oceans between Equator and Subtropical Convergence
ranges.Fregetta maoriana: breeds Little Barrier Island (northern North Island, New Zealand); ranges to seas off southeastern Australia and Fiji
ranges.Fregetta tropica: breeds circumpolar subantarctic islands of South Georgia, Antarctic Peninsula, Bouvetoya (southwest of Africa), Tristan da Cunha perhaps including Gough Island (south-central Atlantic Ocean); Prince Edward, Crozet, and Kerguelen (southwestern to southeastern Indian Ocean), Bounty, Antipodes, and Auckland islands (southeast and south of South Island, New Zealand); non-breeders range southern oceans mostly south of Equator to Antarctic Convergence
ranges.Hydrobates pelagicus: islets of northeastern North Atlantic from southern Iceland and central Norway to northern Spain, Canary Islands, western Africa, and western and north-central Mediterranean Sea
ranges.Hydrobates furcatus: breeds islands off northern Kuril and Commander islands (southeastern Russia), Aleutians, and Gulf of Alaska to northern California; non-breeders range to northeastern coast of Japan, southern Sea of Okhotsk, northern Bering Sea, and central Californian coast
ranges.Hydrobates jabejabe: breeds in winter on Cabo Verde; present all year around Cabo Verde, and extent of at-sea range unknown, possibly to eastern North America
ranges.Hydrobates castro: breeds on northeastern Atlantic islands, islets near St. Helena and Ascension islands, in Pacific off central Japan (northeastern Honshu), Hawaiian Islands (Kauai), and the Galapagos; ranges in Atlantic to Gulf Stream, Gulf of Mexico, western Africa including Gulf of Guinea, in North Pacific, seas off Japan, the Marquesas Islands, near the main Hawaiian Islands, and coasts of southern Central America to northwestern South America
ranges.Hydrobates monteiroi: breeds in summer on Azores; present Azores mainly April-August, and extent of at-sea range unknown, possibly to eastern North America
ranges.Hydrobates melania: breeds islands off California and Baja California, including Gulf of California, from Channel Islands southward to Islas de San Benito (off central Baja California); ranges coastal waters northward to central California and southward to northern Peru
ranges.Hydrobates markhami: breeds off Paracas Peninsula (southern Peru) and Atacama Desert to mountains 50 km inland between Arica and Iquique (northern Chile); ranges east-central Pacific to coasts of southern Mexico, Galápagos, and central Chile
ranges.Hydrobates microsoma: breeds Islas San Benito (central Baja California) and islands in Gulf of California; ranges coastal waters from southern California to Ecuador
ranges.Hydrobates tethys: breeds islands of northern Galapagos and off coasts of central Peru and north-central Chile; non-breeders range from coastal central Baja California (including southern Gulf of California, northwestern Mexico) to northern Chile, and tropical Pacific to southeast of Hawaiian Islands
ranges.Hydrobates hornbyi: breeds Atacama Desert, mostly in mountains well inland (northern Chile); ranges Humboldt Current of southern Ecuador to north-central Chile
ranges.Hydrobates homochroa: breeds islands off California and northern Baja California, from Mendocino County (northwestern California) patchily southward to Isla Todos Santos (northwestern Baja California); ranges coastal California Current to northern California (including Monterey Bay) and north-central Baja California
ranges.Hydrobates tristrami: breeds Izu, Ogasawara (Bonin), and at least formerly Iwo (Volcano) Islands (southern Japan), and Northwestern Hawaiian Islands; ranges eastern coastal waters of Japan and eastward to Hawaiian Islands (Kauai)
ranges.Hydrobates monorhis: breeds mainly islands off Honshu, Japan, also islets off southeastern Russia, Korean Peninsula, eastern China, and Taiwan; ranges through eastern Indonesian Archipelago to southern India and Sri Lanka, Arabian Sea, and off northeastern African coast; recent records from Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean
ranges.Hydrobates matsudairae: breeds Iwo (Volcano) Islands, possibly also Ogasawara (Bonin) Islands (far southern Japan); disperses westward to Arabian Sea, Seychelles, and off eastern African coast, eastward to western Micronesia, seas of eastern Indonesia, and off northwestern Australia
ranges.Hydrobates macrodactylus: formerly bred Guadalupe Island (Mexico); probably extinct, last reported 1912
ranges.Hydrobates socorroensis: summer breeder on islets off Guadalupe Island (western Mexico); ranges in eastern Pacific north to southern California and southward to ca. 10°N
ranges.Hydrobates cheimomnestes: winter breeder on islets off Guadalupe Island (western Mexico); nonbreeding range poorly known, but apparently disperses southward in eastern Pacific, at least as far as the Galapagos
ranges.Hydrobates leucorhous: breeds northeastern Atlantic from southern Iceland, Faroe Islands, central Norway, Ireland, and Scotland; northwestern Atlantic from southern Labrador to Massachusetts; northwestern Pacific from northeastern Russia and northeastern Japan (Hokkaido and northern Honshu) to Alaska and northern and central Baja California (northwestern Mexico); also off southwestern Africa; non-breeders range to tropical Pacific Ocean mainly north of Tropic of Capricorn, and tropical Atlantic, reaching southern Africa in temperate southeastern Atlantic Ocean
ranges.Pagodroma nivea: breeds satellite islets, coasts and to 440 km inland in Antarctica; non-breeders range near pack-ice in Southern Ocean
ranges.Thalassoica antarctica: breeds Antarctic islets, coasts and mountains to 350 km inland; ranges Southern Ocean mostly near ice, south of Antarctic Convergence
ranges.Daption capense: breeds subantarctic and Antarctic islands and coasts; non-breeders range to tropics in cold waters of Benguela Current of southern Africa, southern Australasia, and Humboldt Current of South America north to Ecuador and southern Brazil
ranges.Macronectes giganteus: breeds islands and coasts of Antarctica to Heard (Indian Ocean) and Macquarie islands (Australia), and off southern Chile and Argentina; ranges coasts and open water of all southern oceans and cold currents, often south of Antarctic Convergence
ranges.Macronectes halli: breeds islands north of Antarctic Convergence from South Georgia to Macquarie (southeast of Australia) and Stewart, Chatham, Antipodes, Auckland, and Campbell islands (New Zealand); ranges coasts and open water of all southern oceans, mostly north of Antarctic Convergence
ranges.Fulmarus glacialoides: circumpolar in Antarctic, breeding islets and coast of Antarctica; ranges southern oceans from pack-ice to Humboldt Current off Chile and Peru
ranges.Fulmarus glacialis: breeds islands and coasts of North Atlantic, bays between Arctic and North Atlantic, and North Pacific including Sea of Okhotsk to Hokkaido (northern Japan) and Bering Sea; non-breeders range to coasts of northwestern Pacific southward to central Japan, northeastern Pacific southward to Baja California (northwestern Mexico), western Atlantic southward to North Carolina, and eastern Atlantic southward to France
ranges.Bulweria bifax: formerly St. Helena Island (South Atlantic); extinct
ranges.Bulweria bulwerii: breeds Azores to Cabo Verde, Round Island (off Mauritius), Ryukyu, Izu, Ogasawara (Bonin), and Iwo (Volcano) islands (southern Japan), islands off southern China, Kiribati, Marquesas Islands, and Northwestern and main Hawaiian islands, including Johnson Atoll; ranges widely in Atlantic, reaching western Africa, widely in tropical Indian Ocean from Mascarenes eastward to New Guinea and northern Australia, and through tropical Pacific
ranges.Bulweria fallax: breeds Socotra (Yemen) and Halaaniyat islands (Oman); ranges mainly northwestern Indian Ocean, including gulfs of Aden and Oman, off eastern Africa to waters of Seychelles and Mascarenes, eastward to western India and off northwestern Australia
ranges.Pseudobulweria macgillivrayi: probably breeds Gau Island (central Fiji); distribution at sea unknown but recorded in Fiji waters
ranges.Pseudobulweria aterrima: breeds montane Réunion (Mascarenes); formerly also Rodrigues, where extirpated; ranges adjacent Indian Ocean to Seychelles, Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Timor Sea (off western Australia)
ranges.Pseudobulweria becki: likely breeds montane southern New Ireland (Bismarck Archipelago); ranges eastern Bismarck Archipelago, widely in Solomon Archipelago, and Vanuatu; also recorded Cenderawasih Bay (northern New Guinea) and north-central Moluccas
ranges.Pseudobulweria rostrata: breeds Grande Terre (New Caledonia), Gau (Fiji; southwestern Polynesia), American Samoa (central Polynesia), Society, Marquesas, and Gambier islands (southeastern Tuamotu Islands; eastern Polynesia); non-breeders range to tropical Pacific Ocean waters off New Guinea and northern Australia, and east-central Pacific coast of Mexico and Central America
ranges.Procellaria cinerea: breeds islets of south temperate and subantarctic oceans from Inaccessible and Gough (Atlantic) to Macquarie Island (southeast of Australia), Campbell and Antipodes islands (south of New Zealand); ranges circumpolar subantarctic waters
ranges.Procellaria parkinsoni: breeds Little and Great Barrier islands (off North Island, New Zealand); ranges to southeastern offshore Australian waters and east-central Pacific off Mexico southward to Ecuador
ranges.Procellaria westlandica: breeds coastal foothills of western South Island (New Zealand); ranges to southeastern Australian waters and Humboldt Current from northern Chile southward to Cape Horn
ranges.Procellaria conspicillata: breeds Inaccessible Island (Tristan da Cunha); ranges to coast of southern Brazil to northern Argentina, and to southwestern Africa
ranges.Procellaria aequinoctialis: breeds islets of south temperate and subantarctic oceans north of Antarctic Convergence from Falkland Islands to southern outlying islands of New Zealand; ranges widely in southern oceans, to southern coasts of southern continents and subantarctic islands
ranges.Calonectris leucomelas: breeds coastal islands from Russian Far East, Korean Peninsula, and Japan to islands off western Taiwan; ranges western Pacific to Philippines, Indonesia, and northern Australia eastward through Melanesia to Micronesia
ranges.Calonectris edwardsii: breeds Cabo Verde; ranges mainly in upwelling systems of tropical and South Atlantic
ranges.Calonectris diomedea: breeds Mediterranean islands and southwestern France; ranges mainly in upwelling systems of tropical eastern Atlantic
ranges.Calonectris borealis: eastern Atlantic, breeding from Azores southward to Canary Islands and eastward to Galicia (northwestern Spain) and Berlengas Islands (off west-central Portugal); ranges widely in Atlantic, but mainly in upwelling systems of the Benguela and Agulhas currents
ranges.Ardenna pacifica: widespread in tropical and subtropical Pacific and Indian oceans, breeding on islets from Seychelles and Mascarenes eastward through Ogasawara (Bonin) and Iwo (Volcano) islands (southern Japan) and northern Australia, thence to Hawaiian Islands (widespread) and Revillagigedo Islands (off central Mexico); ranges from northeastern Africa and Malagasy region eastward to southern Baja California and southward to Panama
ranges.Ardenna bulleri: breeds Poor Knights Islands (off northern North Island, New Zealand); wide trans-Pacific dispersal northward to the Aleutians, also eastern Australia and western South American waters to central Chile
ranges.Ardenna tenuirostris: breeds islets off southern Australia, including Bass Strait and Tasmania; ranges to Antarctic ice edge waters, then to Sea of Okhotsk, Sea of Japan, and Bering Sea (North Pacific Ocean)
ranges.Ardenna grisea: breeds southeastern Australia (including Macquarie Island), New Zealand including associated subantarctic island groups, far southern South America (including the Falkland Islands), and Tristan da Cunha (south Atlantic Ocean); winters northward in North Atlantic to Greenland and northwestern Europe, and in northern Pacific to Gulf of Alaska and western USA
ranges.Ardenna gravis: breeds Tristan da Cunha group (mainly) and Kidney Island (Falkland Islands; few); ranges in Atlantic off southern South America and southern Africa, and northward to southern Greenland and northwestern Europe
ranges.Ardenna carneipes: breeds islets off St. Paul (central Indian Ocean), southern Australia, Lord Howe Island (east of Australia), North Island and Cook Strait (New Zealand); ranges to Arabian Sea, eastern Malagasy region, Sea of Okhotsk and Sea of Japan to Gulf of Alaska and western USA coast (rare)
ranges.Ardenna creatopus: breeds Juan Fernández and Mocha islands off central Chile; ranges inshore and coastal eastern Pacific Ocean waters northward to Gulf of Alaska and southward to southern Chile
ranges.Puffinus nativitatis: breeds eastern Polynesian island groups, in Line, Austral, Marquesas, Gambier, and Pitcairn islands, Hawaiian Islands (Northwestern and islets off main islands), Easter Island, and Salas y Gomez; ranges westward to Micronesia and eastward to coasts of western Mexico southward to Costa Rica
ranges.Puffinus subalaris: breeds islets off larger Galapagos Islands; ranges to waters off west-central Mexico and Central America
ranges.Puffinus gavia: breeds islets of northeastern North Island and Marlborough Sounds (northeastern South Island, New Zealand); ranges to Australian waters
ranges.Puffinus huttoni: breeds montane northeastern South Island (New Zealand); ranges to seas off western, southern, and eastern Australia
ranges.Puffinus puffinus: breeds islands of subarctic, temperate, and subtropical North Atlantic Ocean; non-breeders range to South Atlantic Ocean waters of Brazil and Argentina to Tierra del Fuego and southwestern Africa, mostly over continental shelves
ranges.Puffinus yelkouan: breeds on Mediterranean islands and western Black Sea; ranges throughout Mediterranean and Black Sea and disperses to Atlantic coasts of southwestern Europe and northwestern Africa
ranges.Puffinus lherminieri: breeds Elbow Cay (east of central Abaco, northern Bahamas), Long Cay (Exumas, east-central Bahamas), off northern Cuba, east of Puerto Rico, and the Lesser Antilles (Caribbean Sea); Crab Cay (Providencia Islands, east of Nicaragua); Tiger Cay (Bocos del Toro Archipelago, Caribbean northwestern Panama); islas Los Roques, Orchila, and Los Hermanos (north of central Venezuela); and islets of Fernando de Noronha (east of northern Brazil); non-breeders range to Gulf Stream north to New England (western North Atlantic) and Gulf of Mexico
ranges.Puffinus baroli: breeds Azores, Madeira including Desertas and Salvage islands, and Canary islands; ranges (rarely) to coasts of southwestern Europe and northwestern Africa, and near shelf-slope break off New England (northeastern USA)
ranges.Puffinus boydi: breeds Cabo Verde; ranges (rarely) to Canary Islands, northwestern African coastal waters and Amazon Reef (northeastern South America)
ranges.Puffinus heinrothi: presumably breeds montane Bougainville, Kolombangara, and Rendova (northern and west-central Solomon Archipelago); non-breeders range westward to Flores, Moluccan seas, and Bismarck Archipelago
ranges.Puffinus elegans: breeds Tristan da Cunha and Gough (Atlantic), and Chatham and Antipodes islands (New Zealand); ranges in South Atlantic to Falkland Islands and southwestern Africa, and widely in South Pacific from southern New Zealand to south-central Chilean coast
ranges.Puffinus assimilis: south-central Indian Ocean, islets off southwestern and southern Australia, and outlying islands of New Zealand
ranges.Puffinus bryani: breeds Higashi-jima, northern Ogasawara (Bonin) Islands (southern Japan); ranges southern Japanese waters but originally discovered on Midway Island (Hawaii)
ranges.Puffinus persicus: breeds Khuriya Muriya Islands (south of Oman), Socotra, and Moheli (=Mwali, Comoros); non-breeders range Arabian Sea to Persian Gulf, Gulf of Aden, Red Sea, Comoros (southwestern Indian Ocean), and western coast of India
ranges.Puffinus bailloni: breeds tropical Indian Ocean in Malagasy region and tropical Pacific Ocean from Vanuatu through Austral, Marquesas, and Gambier islands (eastern Polynesia)
ranges.Puffinus opisthomelas: breeds islands off western coast of Baja California and northern Gulf of Mexico; ranges to central California inshore waters, Gulf of California, and inshore waters of west-central Mexico
ranges.Puffinus bannermani: breeds Ogasawara (Bonin) and Iwo (Volcano) islands (far southern Japan); ranges in Japanese waters
ranges.Puffinus myrtae: breeds Rapa Island (Austral Islands); non-breeding range unknown
ranges.Puffinus auricularis: breeds mountains of Revillagigedo Islands (off western Mexico); ranges to coastal waters from southern Baja California to Oaxaca (western Mexico)
ranges.Puffinus newelli: breeds mountains of Hawaiian Islands (mainly Kauai, but also Molokai, Maui, and Hawaii); ranges to waters south of Japan and Mariana Islands and to southwestern Pacific near New Caledonia, Solomon Archipelago, and Vanuatu
ranges.Pelecanoides garnotii: breeds islets of Humboldt Current zone from Lobos de Tierra (off northern Peru) to Coronel (Bio-Bio region, south-central Chile)
ranges.Pelecanoides georgicus: islands of subantarctic Atlantic, Indian, and southwestern Pacific oceans from South Georgia to Heard Island (south-central South Indian Ocean) and Codfish Island (=Whenua Hou, northwest of Stewart Island, New Zealand)
ranges.Pelecanoides magellani: breeds islets in Chilean fjords to Cape Horn; ranges coasts and fjords northward to south-central Chile and coastal Santa Cruz (southeastern Argentina)
ranges.Pelecanoides urinatrix: breeds islands of subtropical to subantarctic Atlantic, Indian, and southwestern Pacific; non-breeders range temperate and subantarctic southern oceans around southern South America and to southeast of New Zealand region
ranges.Halobaena caerulea: breeds islands of subantarctic Atlantic and Indian oceans mostly south of Antarctic Convergence from Diego Ramírez (south of Tierra del Fuego), Cape Horn, and South Georgia through subantarctic islands of southern Indian Ocean to Macquarie Island (southeast of Australia); forages to Antarctic waters; disperses to waters of southern South America and southern Australia
ranges.Pachyptila turtur: breeds scattered subtropical and subantarctic islands
ranges.Pachyptila crassirostris: Heard Island (south-central Indian Ocean) and outlying New Zealand islands
ranges.Pachyptila vittata: breeds islands off New Zealand and Tristan da Cunha group; disperses southern oceans
ranges.Pachyptila macgillivrayi: breeds in the southern Atlantic Ocean (Gough Island) and the southern Indian Ocean (off St. Paul Island, formerly also Amsterdam Island); at-sea distribution not well known
ranges.Pachyptila belcheri: breeds Crozet, Kerguelen, Noir (off southern Chile), and Falkland islands; ranges southern oceans to Humboldt Current of western South America, off coast to southern Brazil, and southern Australasia
ranges.Pachyptila desolata: breeds islets of subantarctic to Antarctic oceans (mainly south of Antarctic Convergence), from Antarctic Peninsula to north of Ross Sea, Macquarie (Australia), and Auckland Islands; ranges from pack-ice to waters off southern South America, Africa, and Australasia
ranges.Pachyptila salvini: breeds Prince Edward and Crozet islands; ranges to southern Indian Ocean and southern Australasian seas
ranges.Aphrodroma brevirostris: breeds South Georgia, Gough, Inaccessible, Prince Edward, Crozet, and Kerguelen islands; ranges subantarctic and Antarctic waters north of pack-ice
ranges.Pterodroma mollis: breeds subtropical to subantarctic islands of South Indian and South Atlantic oceans, from Tristan da Cunha and Gough to Maatsuyker (off Tasmania), Macquarie Island (southeast of Australia), and Antipodes Islands (south of New Zealand); ranges to southern waters off Australasia, Africa, and South America
ranges.Pterodroma magentae: breeds only in forest of southern Chatham Island; ranges to Pitcairn group, Juan Fernandez and Nazca Ridge off South America; rare, population about 200
ranges.Pterodroma incerta: breeds Gough and (at least formerly) Tristan da Cunha; ranges to deep offshore waters of southern Brazil to Argentina, and southwestern Africa
ranges.Pterodroma gouldi: breeds on headlands and islands off northern North Island (New Zealand), especially Moutohora Island and Hongiora Island (Bay of Plenty); non-breeding range in deep subtropical water from Tasman Sea (off southeastern Australia) to southern Melanesian waters (southwestern Pacific Ocean)
ranges.Pterodroma lessonii: breeds subantarctic islands of South Indian and South Pacific oceans, from Crozet to Antipodes and Auckland islands; ranges to southern waters off South America, Africa, Australasia, and Antarctica
ranges.Pterodroma macroptera: breeds on subtropical to temperate islands from Tristan da Cunha and Gough (south-central South Atlantic Ocean) to Kerguelen Island (southern Indian Ocean), and Eclipse and Coffin islands (off southwestern Australia); non-breeding range in subtropical to temperate South Atlantic and southern Indian oceans from east of southern South America to southern Australian waters
ranges.Pterodroma hasitata: breeds montane Hispaniola ("Dark-faced") and Dominica ("White-faced"), perhaps also southeastern Cuba and northeastern Jamaica; extinct as a breeder Guadeloupe; ranges to Gulf Stream off southern Canada to North Carolina and throughout Caribbean
ranges.Pterodroma caribbaea: formerly bred montane eastern Jamaica; probably extinct ca. 1936
ranges.Pterodroma cahow: breeds Nonsuch Island (Bermuda); disperses to Gulf Stream
ranges.Pterodroma madeira: breeds in summer in cliffs high on Pico do Arieiro (central Madeira); non-breeding range in subtropical and tropical Atlantic to Azores, St. Helena, and northeastern Brazil (tropical South Atlantic Ocean)

ranges.Manacus candei: Gulf lowlands of southern Mexico to eastern Costa Rica
ranges.Manacus aurantiacus: Pacific slope of southern Costa Rica and western Panama (east to Azuero Peninsula)

ranges.Machaeropterus deliciosus: west slope of Andes of southwestern Colombia and western Ecuador
ranges.Machaeropterus pyrocephalus: tropical rainforest and humid forest in the Orinoco basin and Guiana Shield of central to southern Venezuela and far northern Brazil southward patchily across the Amazon basin from northeastern Brazil (Amapá), to the Cerrado in central Brazil (Goiás), northern Bolivia, and westward to eastern Peru (north to San Martin)

ranges.Machaeropterus eckelberryi: northern Peru: very local on ridgecrests of Andean foothills in eastern San Martín and southwestern Loreto

ranges.Pipreola intermedia: humid montane forest in the eastern Andes from northern Peru south of the Río Marañón, southward to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz)

ranges.Pipreola pulchra: Andes of eastern Peru (Amazonas to Cordillera Vilcabamba of Cusco)

ranges.Carpornis cucullata: southeastern Brazil (Espírito Santo to Rio Grande do Sul)

ranges.Pachyramphus polychopterus: humid to semi-humid forest and woodland, gallery forest, and river islands from northern Guatemala, Belize, and adjacent Mexico southward to northern Colombia, northern Venezuela, Trinidad and Tobago, and the Guianas, and southward across the Orinoco and Amazon basins, in interior Colombia southward along the Cauca and Magdalena valleys, west of the Andes southward along the foothills of the Andes to northwestern Ecuador, and the Cerrado, Caatinga, and Atlantic Forest regions to northern Argentina
ranges.Pachyramphus marginatus: tropical rainforest in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from central and eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to northern Bolivia and in the Atlantic Forest from northeastern Brazil, in Paraiba, southward to northern Santa Catarina
ranges.Pachyramphus albogriseus: humid foothill and montane forest in the mountains of Costa Rica and western Panama, in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela, Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Sierra de Perijá, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward along the eastern Andes of Colombia to southeastern Peru, in Cusco

ranges.Pachyramphus versicolor: humid montane forest in the mountains of Costa Rica and western Panama, the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Sierra de Perijá, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward to northern Peru north of the Río Marañón, and Peru south and east of the Río Marañón southward along the eastern Andes to central Bolivia
ranges.Pachyramphus viridis: humid tropical, foothill, and montane forest and borders in the eastern Andes from southern Colombia southward to southeastern Peru, in the Guiana Shield of eastern Venezuela and adjacent Guyana, in lower Amazon basin in northeastern Brazil, and in the Cerrado, Caatinga, and Atlantic Forest regions from northeastern Brazil southward to eastern Bolivia, northeastern Argentina, Uruguay, and Paraguay; in the Yungas of Bolivia also southward to northwestern Argentina and in the southern Amazon basin westward to southwestern Brazil, adjacent Peru, and northern Bolivia
ranges.Pachyramphus spodiurus: Pacific lowlands of western Ecuador and far northwestern Peru
ranges.Pachyramphus rufus: dry to humid woodland, scrub, riparian groves, and mangroves from eastern Panama eastward to northern Venezuela, southward in interior Colombia along the ríos Cauca and Magdalena and east of the Andes in the llanos of southwestern Venezuela and northeastern Colombia; and from the Guianas southward in the Amazon basin of Brazil to western Tocantins and northern Mato Grosso and westward to northeastern Peru and far southeastern Colombia
ranges.Pachyramphus minor: southern Venezuela and the Guianas to eastern Bolivia and Amazonian Brazil
ranges.Pachyramphus validus: semi-humid to dry woodland and humid montane forest in the Amazon basin south of the Amazon River and in the Cerrado, Caatinga, and Atlantic Forest regions from northeastern Brazil southward to eastern Bolivia, eastern Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, and northernmost Uruguay; also in the foothills of the Andes from southeastern Peru southward to northwestern Argentina

ranges.Oxyruncus cristatus: humid lowland to premontane forest in the mountains of Costa Rica and western Panama, in easternmost Panama and adjacent Colombia southward to Serrania de Baudo, and in the northern end of the central and western Andes of Colombia and Serrania de San Lucas; east of the Andes in the tepuis and montane areas of southeastern Venezuela, the Guianas and northernmost Brazil, locally in the eastern Andes of southeastern Ecuador southward to western Bolivia, and also locally in the lower Amazon basin in northeastern Brazil, south of the Amazon River (in the lower Rio Tocantins and Serra do Carajas), and in the Atlantic Forest region from northeastern Brazil (Alagoas, southward to northern Rio Grande do Norte, and western Paraná), northeastern Argentina, and eastern Paraguay
ranges.Onychorhynchus swainsoni: southeastern Brazil (Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, and Paraná)
ranges.Onychorhynchus coronatus: humid, semi-humid and dry forest, gallery forest from southeastern Mexico (including Yucatan Peninsula), and Pacific slope from western Costa Rica, southward to eastern Panama, northern Colombia and western Venezuela, southward in interior Colombia to the middle Cauca and Magdalena valleys, and from northwestern Ecuador southward to northwestern Peru; east of the Andes from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward across the Amazon basin to south-central Brazil and northern Bolivia
ranges.Terenotriccus erythrurus: humid forest from southeeastern Mexico, northern Guatemala and Belize southward across most Central America to eastern Panama; in northern Colombia and western Venezuela southward to the middle Magdalena Valley and along the Pacific lowlands southward to southwestern Ecuador; east of the Andes in the coastal mountains of north-central Venezuela, the Orinoco basin from eastern Venezuela, and the Guianas southward across the Amazon basin to central Bolivia
ranges.Myiobius atricaudus: humid to semi-humid and deciduous forest and woodland in southeastern Costa Rica and Panama, northern Colombia southward along the Cauca and Magdalena valleys, the Pacific lowlands southward to southwestern Ecuador and adjacent Peru, east of the Andes in the middle to low Orinoco Valley of Venezuela, and in the Amazon basin from southeastern Colombia southward to east-central Peru, eastward locally in the southern Amazonian Brazil, and the Cerrado, Caatinga, and Atlantic Forest regions (northeastern Brazil southward to São Paulo and adjacent Santa Catarina)
ranges.Myiobius barbatus: humid forest in the middle Magdalena Valley in northern Colombia, and east of the Andes in the Orinoco basin of eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward across the Amazon basin to southeastern Peru, southwestern Brazil and northernmost Bolivia; also in the Atlantic Forest region from northeastern Brazil southward to southeastern Brazil in northern Santa Catarina and locally in interior Brazil, in eastern Goiás and western Minas Gerais
ranges.Myiobius sulphureipygius: humid to semi-humid forest and woodland from the Gulf of Mexico slope in southeastern Mexico and Yucatan Peninsula, southward along the Caribbean slope to eastern Panama and in the Pacific slope of Costa Rica and Panama, and from northwestern Colombia southward along the Pacific lowlands southward to southwestern Ecuador and adjacent Peru
ranges.Myiobius villosus: humid foothill and montane forest in the Cerro Tacarcuna in easternmost Panama, in the Sierra de Perijá and the Andes of western Venezuela southward along the eastern Andes to western Bolivia, and in the western Andes from northern Colombia, including the northern end of the central Andes, southward to southwestern Ecuador
ranges.Piprites pileata: locally from southeastern Brazil (Rio de Janeiro) to northeastern Argentina
ranges.Piprites griseiceps: Caribbean lowlands of eastern Guatemala to Costa Rica
ranges.Piprites chloris: humid forest in the lower Cauca and middle Magdalena valleys of northern Colombia and in the foothills of Sierra de Perijá eastward locally to the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela eastward to the Paría Peninsula, and in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern and southern Venezuela and the Guianas southward across the entire Amazon basin to central Bolivia; also in the Atlantic Forest region from northeastern Brazil, in Pernambuco and Alagoas southward to Santa Catarina, Paraná, adjacent Rio Grande do Sul, northeastern Argentina, and eastern Paraguay
ranges.Neopipo cinnamomea: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin and Guiana Shield from easternmost and southern Venezuela and the Guianas southwestward across the Amazon basin to southeastern Colombia, eastern Ecuador and Peru to the foothills of the Andes in western Bolivia; in Brazil southward to northern and western Mato Grosso and Rondônia, and eastward to central Para
ranges.Calyptura cristata: southeastern Brazil (Rio de Janeiro area); undocumented since 1860 and probably extinct
ranges.Platyrinchus coronatus: humid forest from the Gulf of Mexico slope in northern Honduras southeastward to Panama and the Pacific slope of southeastern Costa Rica and western Panama, in the lower Cauca and middle Magdalena valleys of northern Colombia, west of the Andes southward to northwestern Ecuador, and east of the Andes in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward across Amazonia to northern Bolivia (western Beni) and Brazil (eastward to central Pará)
ranges.Platyrinchus platyrhynchos: tropical rainforest in the Río Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward across the entire Amazon basin to northern Bolivia, Rondônia and northern Mato Grosso, and west to eastern Ecuador and Peru
ranges.Platyrinchus leucoryphus: southeastern Brazil (Espírito Santo) to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
ranges.Platyrinchus flavigularis: montane cloudforest in coastal mountains of north-central Venezuela (Carabobo), the Sierra de Perijá, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward along the eastern Andes of Colombia (and locally in the western Andes in southwestern Colombia) to northernmost Peru north of the Río Marañón, and in the eastern Andes of northern Peru south of the Marañón (southward to Cusco and adjacent Ayacucho)
ranges.Platyrinchus cancrominus: tropical southern Mexico to western Costa Rica and northwestern Panama
ranges.Platyrinchus saturatus: tropical rainforest, mainly in sandy-soil and black-water forest, in the Río Orinoco and Amazon basins from southern Venezuela and the Guianas southward across the Amazon basin to northern Mato Grosso and northeastern Rondônia, Brazil, and westward to eastern Colombia, northeastern Ecuador and northeastern Peru
ranges.Platyrinchus mystaceus: humid foothill to montane forest from western Costa Rica and adjacent Nicaragua southeastward to eastern Panama and adjacent Colombia, the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela eastward to Trinidad and Tobago and the Guianas, and southward to the tepuis of southern Venezuela, adjacent Guyana, and northernmost Brazil, Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Sierra de Perijá, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward to northern Peru, and the eastern Andes from northern Peru southeastward to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz), and interior and eastern Brazil (northern Maranhão and Piauí southward to Rio Grande do Sul), eastern Paraguay, and northeastern Argentina
ranges.Tachuris rubrigastra: freshwater marshes with extensive reedbeds on the coast from northern Peru, in Piura, southward to southern Chile, and in the Andes from south-central Peru southward across Bolivia to northwestern Argentina; also in the pampas and grasslands from southeastern Brazil southward across Uruguay to southern Argentina, where seasonal; winters northward to northeastern Argentina, eastern Paraguay and southeastern Brazil
ranges.Corythopis delalandi: southern Brazil to eastern Bolivia, eastern Paraguay, and northeastern Argentina
ranges.Corythopis torquatus: tropical rainforest in the Río Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southwest and southward across the entire Amazon basin to eastern Ecuador and Peru, central Bolivia, central Mato Grosso, western Tocantins, eastern Pará and adjacent Maranhão
ranges.Pseudotriccus ruficeps: Andes of Colombia to western Bolivia (La Paz and Cochabamba)
ranges.Pseudotriccus simplex: east slope of Andes of southern Peru (Puno) and western Bolivia
ranges.Pseudotriccus pelzelni: humid foothill and montane cloudforest in the Cerro Pirre and Cerro Tacarcuna in far eastern Panama and adjacent Colombia, and in the western and central Andes of Colombia southward to northernmost Peru, in the eastern Andes of Colombia only on the eastern slope from Cundinamarca and southward, also in the eastern Andes of Peru from Amazonas and San Martín southeastward to Ayacucho and Cusco
ranges.Leptopogon rufipectus: Andes of Colombia to eastern Ecuador, western Venezuela, and northern Peru
ranges.Leptopogon taczanowskii: east slope of Andes of Peru (Amazonas to Cusco)
ranges.Leptopogon superciliaris: semi-deciduous to humid foothill and montane forest from western Costa Rica eastward to eastern Panama,coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Falcón eastward to the Paría Peninsula), Trinidad, the Sierra de Perijá, the Andes from western Venezuela southward along the western, central, and eastern Andes of Colombia to northern Peru north of the Río Marañón (in western Ecuador down to the coastal lowlands), and in the eastern Andes from northern Peru southeastward to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz and northern Chuquisaca)
ranges.Leptopogon amaurocephalus: semi-deciduous, gallery and humid forest from the Gulf of Mexico slope in southeastern Mexico southeastward to northern Costa Rica, and in the Pacific lowlands of western Panama and adjacent Costa Rica; in northern Colombia and western Venezuela southward to the middle Cauca and Magdalena valleys, and east of the Andes in the Amazon basin from western Venezuela southward to central Bolivia, westward across southern Brazil and southward along the Yungas to northwestern Argentina; in the Guiana Shield and Orinoco basin in eastern Venezuela, the Guianas and northern Brazil (Roraima and Amapá), and in interior and eastern Brazil from northern Maranhão, Piauí and Rio Grande do Norte southward to eastern Bolivia, eastern Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, and northernmost Uruguay
ranges.Mionectes striaticollis: montane cloudforest in the Andes from northern Colombia southward to northern Peru, and in the eastern Andes from northern Peru southeastward to southern Bolivia (Chuquisaca)
ranges.Mionectes olivaceus: foothills and highlands of Costa Rica and western Panama (to Chiriquí and Ngäbe-Buglé), humid lowland and foothill forest from central Panama eastward to northwestern Colombia, southward to the headwaters of the Río Cauca and Río Magdalena, southward along the Pacific lowlands to northwestern Ecuador and along the foothills of the Andes to southwestern Ecuador; east of the Andes in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela eastward to the Paría Peninsula and Trinidad, and in the Andes from western Venezuela southward to western Bolivia

ranges.Mionectes rufiventris: southeastern Brazil (Espírito Santo) to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
ranges.Mionectes roraimae: tepuis of southern and southeastern Venezuela, adjacent northern Brazil, and western Guyana
ranges.Mionectes macconnelli: tropical rainforest in the Guiana Shield and the eastern Amazon basin from eastern Venezuela southeastward across the Guianas to northeastern Brazil, to southern Pará and eastern Amazonas, east of the Rio Negro; also in southeastern Peru, adjacent Brazil and northwestern Bolivia southward to western Santa Cruz
ranges.Pogonotriccus difficilis: coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil (Espírito Santo to northern Rio Grande do Sul)
ranges.Pogonotriccus eximius: southeastern Brazil (Espírito Santo) to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
ranges.Pogonotriccus lanyoni: central Andes of northern Colombia (Antioquia and eastern Caldas)
ranges.Pogonotriccus ophthalmicus: foothill and montane cloudforest in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Falcón eastward to Miranda), the western and central Andes from northern Colombia (including Serranía de San Lucas) southward to northwestern Ecuador, and the eastern Andes from southern Colombia southward to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz)
ranges.Pogonotriccus paulista: southeastern Brazil (Espírito Santo) to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
ranges.Pogonotriccus poecilotis: Andes of northern Colombia to western Venezuela, eastern Ecuador, and southern Peru
ranges.Pogonotriccus venezuelanus: coastal cordillera of northern Venezuela (Carabobo to Distrito Federal)
ranges.Pogonotriccus orbitalis: Andes of far southern Colombia to Ecuador, Peru, and western Bolivia
ranges.Pogonotriccus chapmani: tepuis of southern Venezuela and adjacent southwestern Guyana, and far northern Brazil

ranges.Phylloscartes flavovirens: Pacific lowlands of Panama (Canal Zone to eastern Darién)
ranges.Phylloscartes virescens: lowlands of the Guianas and adjacent northern Brazil (Amazonas)
ranges.Phylloscartes kronei: coastal southeastern Brazil (southeastern São Paulo to northeastern Santa Catarina)
ranges.Phylloscartes beckeri: montane forest of southeastern Brazil (southern Bahia near Boa Nova)

ranges.Phylloscartes sylviolus: southeastern Brazil (Espírito Santo) to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
ranges.Phylloscartes roquettei: south-central Bahia to central Minas Gerais, in eastern Brazil
ranges.Phylloscartes superciliaris: humid montane and foothill forest in the mountains of Costa Rica and locally in Panama and adjacent Colombia; also in the Sierra de Perijá and patchily across the northern part of the western, central and eastern Andes of Colombia, eastern Andes of Ecuador and adjacent northeastern Peru
ranges.Phylloscartes nigrifrons: tepuis of southern Venezuela (southern Bolívar and Amazonas)
ranges.Phylloscartes gualaquizae: east slope of Andes of eastern Ecuador and northern Peru (San Martín)
ranges.Phylloscartes parkeri: Andean foothills of central and southeastern Peru and adjacent northern Bolivia
ranges.Rhynchocyclus pacificus: western Colombia (Chocó) to northwestern Ecuador (south to southern Pichincha)

ranges.Tolmomyias traylori: tropical southern Colombia and northeastern Peru north of the Amazon
ranges.Tolmomyias flaviventris: dry to humid forest, woodland and scrub, sandy-soil savanna, and gallery forest and mangrove from eastern Panama eastward across northern Colombia and western Venezuela, in interior Colombia southward along the Magdalena Valley to Cundinamarca; east of the Andes in northern Venezuela eastward to Trinidad and Tobago and the Guianas southward to northeastern Colombia, most Amazonia in Brazil to northern Bolivia, and in interior and eastern Brazil southward to southern Rio de Janeiro, southern Minas Gerais, and Goiás

ranges.Taeniotriccus andrei: mangrove edges, bamboo-dominated forest, riparian thickets, and varzea forest in the Orinoco basin in eastern Venezuela and adjacent northwestern Guyana southward to northern Brazil (Roraima), and in the eastern Amazon basin, south of the Amazon River (eastern Pará, western Maranhão, northern Tocantins and northernmost Mato Grosso)

ranges.Cnipodectes subbrunneus: lowlands of eastern Panama to western Colombia and western Ecuador, and southeastern Colombia to eastern Ecuador, eastern Peru, northwestern Bolivia, and western Amazonian Brazil
ranges.Todirostrum maculatum: dense riparian thickets in river islands, oxbow lakes, and mangrove edge from southeastern Colombia southward to northwestern Bolivia, and eastward across the Amazon of Brazil to northeastern Mato Grosso, western Tocantins, northern and western Maranhão, and adjacent Piauí, and northward to the coast of the Guianas, northeastern Venezuela, and Trinidad

ranges.Todirostrum poliocephalum: lowlands of southeastern Brazil (southern Minas Gerais to eastern Santa Catarina)
ranges.Todirostrum nigriceps: Caribbean slope of Costa Rica to western Ecuador and northwestern Venezuela
ranges.Todirostrum pictum: southern Venezuela to the Guianas and northern Brazil (east of Rio Negro)
ranges.Todirostrum chrysocrotaphum: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin from eastern Colombia southward to central Bolivia and southeastward across Amazonian Brazil, south of the Amazon River from the Rio Negro to the east, to northern Mato Grosso, eastern Pará, adjacent Tocantins and western Maranhão

ranges.Poecilotriccus albifacies: southeastern Peru (Madre de Dios and Cusco), western Brazil (Acre), and northern Bolivia (Pando)

ranges.Poecilotriccus pulchellus: humid foothills of southeastern Peru (Cusco and Puno)
ranges.Poecilotriccus luluae: northern Peru (Cordillera de Colán) and adjacent eastern Andes
ranges.Poecilotriccus ruficeps: montane cloudforest and scrub dominated by bamboo in the Sierra de Perijá and the Andes from western Venezuela southward along the Andes of Colombia to northern Peru north of the Río Marañón, in Piura and Cajamarca
ranges.Poecilotriccus plumbeiceps: humid forest borders and scrub, bamboo stands, and bracken thickets in the Andes of southeastern Peru southward across Bolivia to northwestern Argentina, to Salta and Tucuman, in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil from Pernambuco southward to Rio Grande do Sul and adjacent Uruguay, and inland to western Paraná, northeastern Argentina, and western Paraguay
ranges.Poecilotriccus senex: central Amazonian Brazil (Madeira drainage in Amazonas and Rondônia)
ranges.Poecilotriccus russatus: tepuis of southeastern Venezuela and northern Brazil (Cerro Uei-tepui in Roraima)
ranges.Poecilotriccus sylvia: Gulf slope of southern Mexico (Veracruz) southward to Panama (Canal Zone), tropical northern Colombia (Cauca and Magdalena valleys) to northwestern Venezuela (eastward to northern Bolívar), and the Guianas and northern Brazil (Rio Branco to northern Piauí)
ranges.Poecilotriccus fumifrons: dense humid to semi-humid scrub, bushes, and thickets in Suriname and French Guiana southward across the easternmost Amazon basin in Brazil to northern Mato Grosso, and in the Cerrado of Brazil from northern Maranhão, Piauí, and Ceará southward to southern Tocantins, and in far southern Venezuela; also in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil from Rio Grande do Norte southward to southern Bahia
ranges.Poecilotriccus latirostris: dense thickets in shrub in forest edges, riparian, and gallery forest in the Amazon basin from southeastern Colombia southeastward to northern and eastern Bolivia, far northern Paraguay, and in Brazil mainly south of the Amazon River eastward to the Rio Tapajós in central Pará, western and southern Tocantins, Goiás, western Minas Gerais, and southeastward to western São Paulo, Mato Grosso do Sul, and adjacent Paraná
ranges.Hemitriccus minor: vine tangles inside tropical rainforest and varzea forest in the southern Amazon basin, mostly south of the Amazon River from central Brazil (Amazonas and Pará) southwestward to western Acre, southward to southwestern Mato Grosso, northern and northeastern Bolivia, and eastward to northern and western Tocantins; in northern Brazil north of the Amazon River along both banks of the Rio Negro
ranges.Hemitriccus spodiops: Yungas of southeastern Peru (Puno) and Bolivia (southward to western Santa Cruz)
ranges.Hemitriccus cohnhafti: southwestern Amazonia in Brazil (eastern Acre), adjacent southeastern Peru (Madre de Dios), and far northeastern Bolivia
ranges.Hemitriccus flammulatus: mostly bamboo thickets inside tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin of southeastern Peru (Ucayali, Cusco, Madre de Dios, and northern Puno), and disjunctly in northern San Martin southward to northern and central Bolivia (to western Santa Cruz), and southwestern Brazil (Acre eastward to western Mato Grosso)
ranges.Hemitriccus diops: southeastern Brazil (southeastern Bahia) to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
ranges.Hemitriccus obsoletus: humid forest and bamboo patches in the Atlantic Forest of southeastern Brazil in southern Minas Gerais and southern Rio de Janeiro southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul, and far northeastern Argentina
ranges.Hemitriccus josephinae: southern Guyana to Suriname, French Guiana, and northern Brazil (Amapá)
ranges.Hemitriccus zosterops: tropical rainforest and woodland in the Amazon basin from southeastern Colombia southward to northeastern Peru, to Ucayali and adjacent Huánuco and Pasco, and eastward north of the Amazon River in Brazil, southern Venezuela and southern Guyana to northeastern Brazil, Suriname and French Guiana
ranges.Hemitriccus griseipectus: tropical rainforest, varzea forest, and woodland from far eastern Peru southward to northern Bolivia, foothills of the Andes to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz), and eastward across Amazonian Brazil, south of the Amazon River (to east-central Pará and adjacent Tocantins), and the Atlantic Forest region of northeastern Brazil (Rio Grande do Norte southward to Alagoas)
ranges.Hemitriccus orbitatus: lowlands of southeastern Brazil (southern Minas Gerais to northeastern Rio Grande do Sul)
ranges.Hemitriccus iohannis: southeastern Colombia to eastern Peru, northern Bolivia, and western Amazonian Brazil
ranges.Hemitriccus striaticollis: humid to semi-humid woodland and scrub, thickets and bamboo stands in the Amazon basin in eastern Colombia, locally in dry valleys in eastern Peru and in the Cerrado and Caatinga from northeastern Brazil, in northern Maranhão and adjacent Pará southwestward to northern Mato Grosso do Sul and northern Bolivia; also in southern Amazonia in Brazil, south of the Amazon River, west to eastern Amazonas and north to central Pará, and in the Atlantic Forest from Rio Grande do Norte southward to central Bahia
ranges.Hemitriccus nidipendulus: humid forest and restinga in the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado regions of eastern Brazil from Sergipe and northern and interior Bahia southward to southern Paraná and adjacent Santa Catarina
ranges.Hemitriccus margaritaceiventer: arid to semiarid scrub, riparian thickets, scrub, and savanna in the lowlands of northern Colombia and northern Venezuela Iincluding Isla Margarita), southward in interior Colombia along the Magdalena Valley, the tepuis of southern and eastern Venezuela, adjacent Guyana, and northernmost Brazil, Sierra de Chiribiquete in eastern Colombia, and locally in dry valleys of eastern Peru and northwestern Bolivia; also in the Cerrado and Caatinga from northeastern Brazil southwestward to eastern Bolivia, Paraguay, and northernmost Uruguay, to northern Argentina, southward to northern Buenos Aires, San Luis, and Córdoba, and locally in southern Amazonia west to eastern Amazonas and Rondônia

ranges.Hemitriccus minimus: local in western Amazonia (Ecuador in Pastaza; Peru in eastern Loreto); more widespread from northeastern Bolivia across central and eastern Amazonian Brazil
ranges.Hemitriccus granadensis: montane cloudforest in the coastal mountains of central-north Venezuela, and in the Sierra de Perijá, Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta and the Andes from far western Venezuela southward along the western and central Andes of Colombia to far northwestern Ecuador, and along the eastern Andes of Colombia and Ecuador to the eastern Andes of Peru and southeastward to northwestern Bolivia, to Cochabamba
ranges.Hemitriccus cinnamomeipectus: southern Ecuador (Cordillera del Cóndor) to northern Peru (San Martín)
ranges.Hemitriccus mirandae: lowlands of eastern Brazil (Ceará, Pernambuco, and Alagoas)
ranges.Hemitriccus rufigularis: foothills on east slope of Andes in Ecuador, Peru, and western Bolivia
ranges.Hemitriccus furcatus: southeastern Brazil (Rio de Janeiro, southern Minas Gerais, and northeastern São Paulo)
ranges.Myiornis auricularis: humid forest in the Atlantic Forest, Caatinga and Cerrado regions of eastern Brazil from Pernambuco southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul, eastward southern Goiás and southern Mato Grosso do Sul, eastern Paraguay, and northeastern Argentina
ranges.Myiornis albiventris: east slope of Andes of Peru (Huánuco) to western Bolivia (Santa Cruz)
ranges.Myiornis atricapillus: humid lowlands of Costa Rica to western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador

ranges.Atalotriccus pilaris: tropical dry to semi-humid forest, scrub, thickets and woodland in the Pacific lowlands of western to central Panama, and in the lowlands of northern Colombia and western Venezuela; in interior Colombia southward to the upper basin of the Río Magdalena; east of the Andes in northern to central Venezuela southwestward to the llanos of northeastern Colombia, southward to southern Meta, and in the Serrania de Chiribiquete; also locally in the Guiana Shield in southern Guyana and far northern Brazil, in Roraima
ranges.Lophotriccus pileatus: semi-deciduous to humid forest and bamboo stands in foothills of montane regions from eastern Honduras southeastward to eastern Panama and adjacent Colombia; in the Sierra de Perijá and the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (from Falcón eastward to Miranda), and in the Andes from western Panama southward to northern Peru, and in the eastern Andes southward to southeastern Peru, in Puno; in western Ecuador and adjacent northwestern Peru and southwestern Colombia down to lowlands

ranges.Lophotriccus galeatus: eastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, the Guianas, and northern Amazonian Brazil

ranges.Oncostoma olivaceum: tropical eastern Panama and northern Colombia (eastward to Santa Marta region)

ranges.Attila torridus: far southwestern Colombia to western Ecuador and northwestern Peru (Tumbes)
ranges.Attila citriniventris: eastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, northeastern Peru (Loreto), and western Amazonian Brazil
ranges.Attila rufus: humid forest and scrub in the Atlantic Forest region of Brazil from southern Bahia southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul

ranges.Myiodynastes chrysocephalus: east slope of Andes of Peru to Bolivia and northwestern Argentina
ranges.Myiodynastes hemichrysus: montane cloudforest in Costa Rica and western Panama, eastern Panama (Darién), the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Falcón to Monagas), the Santa Marta and Perijá mountains, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward to northern Peru (north of the Río Marañón)

ranges.Myiodynastes maculatus: breeds Gulf slope of Mexico to northwestern Peru (Piura), Caribbean coast of Colombia and Venezuela, the Guianas, and through eastern Peru and central Argentina; northern and southern populations migratory
ranges.Tyrannopsis sulphurea: southern Venezuela, Trinidad, and the Guianas to northern Bolivia and Amazonian Brazil

ranges.Conopias trivirgatus: tropical rainforest disjunctly and sparsely in the Amazon basin in southern Venezuela, far northeastern Ecuador, eastern Peru, western Bolivia, and northern Brazil, mostly along the Amazon River (eastward to western Pará), and in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil (central Bahía southward to northern Santa Catarina), eastern Paraguay, and northeastern Argentina

ranges.Empidonomus aurantioatrocristatus: eastern Brazil (Rio Tapajós to northern Goiás and Piauí) and Bolivia to northern Argentina and southern Brazil; winters northward to western Amazonia

ranges.Tyrannus verticalis: breeds western North America; winters southern Mexico to Costa Rica and (?) Panama
ranges.Muscigralla brevicauda: arid southwestern Ecuador to far northern Chile; Gorgona Island (Colombia)

ranges.Alectrurus risora: locally in eastern Paraguay, southern Brazil, Uruguay, and northern Argentina

ranges.Xenotriccus mexicanus: central Mexico (Michoacán to Oaxaca) and adjacent Guatemala
