ranges.Cranioleuca antisiensis: semi-humid to humid montane forest and woodland, Polylepis woodland, semi-humid scrub in the western Andes (locally in the eastern Andes) from southern Ecuador, from southern Chimborazo, southward to west-central Peru, in Lima; in the eastern Andes of Peru from Amazonas, south and east of the Río Marañón, to Huánuco and Pasco
ranges.Pseudasthenes humicola: xeric scrub, shrubland and sclerophyllous forest from south region of Antofagasta southward to Malleco; one old record from Mendoza, western Argentina
ranges.Pseudasthenes patagonica: southern Argentina (Mendoza southward to northern Santa Cruz)
ranges.Pseudasthenes steinbachi: Andes of western Argentina (western Salta to Mendoza)
ranges.Pseudasthenes cactorum: arid montane scrub in the western foothills and slopes of the Andes in western Peru, from southern La Libertad southward to Arequipa, and inland to Ayacucho and adjacent Moquegua
ranges.Mazaria propinqua: river islands in Amazon basin (the Guianas to Bolivia)
ranges.Schoeniophylax phryganophilus: gallery and riparian scrub and thickets in the Cerrado, Caatinga, and Chaco of interior Brazil, from Piauí southward to Minas Gerais, and inland to western São Paulo, Mato Grosso do Sul, and southern Mato Grosso, and Paraguay, westward to eastern and northern Bolivia, and southward to northern Argentina to northern Buenos Aires, and Uruguay
ranges.Certhiaxis mustelinus: far southeastern Colombia to eastern Peru and Amazonian Brazil
ranges.Certhiaxis cinnamomeus: freshwater marshes in the lowlands of northern Colombia and western Venezuela, southward in the Magdalena Valley (to Huila); east of the Andes in the llanos of southwestern Venezuela and northeastern Colombia eastward across northern Venezuela to Trinidad, the savannas of Guyana and far northern Brazil (Roraima), the Guianas, and northeastern Brazil (Amapá); inland along the Amazon River to far southeastern Colombia and northeastern Peru (west to the middle Río Ucayali), and along the Rio Madeira and tributaries to northern Bolivia and far southeastern Peru, and eastern Brazil (northern Pará southward along the Atlantic Coast and interior Brazil) to eastern Bolivia, Paraguay, northern Argentina (southward to La Pampa and Buenos Aires), and Uruguay
ranges.Synallaxis chinchipensis: northwestern Peru (upper Marañón and Chinchipe valleys)
ranges.Synallaxis zimmeri: west slope of Andes of central Peru (Ancash)
ranges.Synallaxis stictothorax: arid scrub and deciduous woodland edge of lowlands of coastal west-central Ecuador to northwestern Peru
ranges.Synallaxis cinerascens: eastern Paraguay to southeastern Brazil, northern Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
ranges.Synallaxis scutata: deciduous to semi-deciduous forest from northeastern Brazil, in Piauí and Ceará, southwestward across interior Brazil to northern São Paulo, westward across the Caatinga of south-central Brazil to northwestern Paraguay, eastern Bolivia, and southward to northwestern Argentina (southward to Salta); also sparsely in western Bolivia and adjacent Peru
ranges.Synallaxis maranonica: southern Ecuador (Zamora-Chinchipe) to northwestern Peru (northern Cajamarca)
ranges.Synallaxis gujanensis: riparian and gallery forest and shrubland in the Amazon basin from eastern Colombia southward to eastern Bolivia, and eastward across Amazonian Brazil, mostly south of the Amazon River, to northeastern Pará and northern Maranhão; northward across the Amazon River mouth to the Guianas to eastern Venezuela and adjacent northern Brazil, and to the Orinoco basin of central Venezuela west to northeasternmost Colombia
ranges.Synallaxis albilora: eastern Bolivia (eastern Santa Cruz) to interior southwestern Brazil and northern Paraguay
ranges.Synallaxis subpudica: eastern Andes of northern Colombia (Boyacá and Cundinamarca)
ranges.Synallaxis brachyura: forest edge and scrub of lowlands to hills of Caribbean slope from northeastern Honduras to Nicaragua, thence both slopes in Costa Rica and western Panama, disjunctly in central and eastern Panama through Cauca and Magdalena valleys of north-central Colombia, and west of Andes southward to far northern Peru (Tumbes)
ranges.Synallaxis tithys: arid tropical southwestern Ecuador to far northwestern Peru (Tumbes)
ranges.Synallaxis kollari: locally in campos of northern Brazil (Roraima) and (?) adjacent Guyana
ranges.Synallaxis erythrothorax: forest clearings often near water in lowlands and hills of Caribbean slope from central Veracruz, eastern Puebla, and northern Oaxaca, including Yucatan Peninsula (but not Cozumel), through northwestern Honduras, and Pacific slope from southeastern Chiapas through El Salvador
ranges.Synallaxis candei: deciduous forest and scrub in the lowlands of northern Colombia westward to northern Antioquia, southward to the middle Magdalena Valley in northern Santander, and eastward to northwestern Venezuela (incluing the Guajira Peninsula)
ranges.Synallaxis fuscorufa: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
ranges.Synallaxis castanea: coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Aragua to Distrito Federal)
ranges.Synallaxis unirufa: montane cloudforest in the Sierra de Perijá and Andes of western Venezuela southwestward along western, central and eastern Andes of Colombia to southern Peru, to northern Cusco; in the western Andes southward to northwestern Ecuador
ranges.Synallaxis cinnamomea: humid forest in the foothills of Sierra de Perijá, the northeastern Andes of Colombia (southward to northern Meta) and Andes of western Venezuela eastward along the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela to the Paría Peninsula and Trinidad and Tobago

ranges.Synallaxis infuscata: northeastern Brazil (northeastern Maranhão, eastern Pernambuco, and adjacent Alagoas)
ranges.Synallaxis ruficapilla: eastern Paraguay to southeastern Brazil and northeastern Argentina (Misiones)
ranges.Synallaxis cinerea: eastern Brazil (interior and southern Bahia and northeastern Minas Gerais)
ranges.Synallaxis hellmayri: arid northeastern Brazil (Piauí, northern Bahia, and western Pernambuco)
ranges.Synallaxis spixi: southeastern Brazil to eastern Paraguay, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
ranges.Synallaxis hypospodia: locally from southeastern Peru and northern Bolivia to central and northeastern Brazil
ranges.Synallaxis albigularis: tropical rainforest in the western Amazon basin from eastern Colombia southward across Ecuador, Peru and western Brazil (Acre) to far northeastern Bolivia (in La Paz), eastward along the Amazon River to eastern Amazonas, west of the Rio Madeira
ranges.Synallaxis beverlyae: river islands in the upper Río Orinoco of Venezuela
ranges.Synallaxis albescens: shrubland and savanna habitats from southwestern Costa Rica eastward to south-central Panama, in northern Colombia southward along the Cauca and Magdalena valleys (to the upper Río Patía Valley and Huila); eastward across Venezuela (including Isla Margarita), Trinidad, far northern Brazil (Roraima), and the Guianas, and southward along the Atlantic coast of Brazil, interior Brazil, and southern Amazonian Brazil (to Rio Grande do Sul), western Uruguay, Paraguay, eastern and northern Bolivia, far southeastern Peru, and southward to central Argentina (southward to Río Negro), in Amazonian Brazil westward along the Amazon River to far southeastern Colombia and adjacent Peru
ranges.Synallaxis frontalis: deciduous and gallery forest and scrub from northeastern Brazil (Maranhão, Piauí, and Ceará), southward along the Atlantic Coast to Rio Grande do Sul and Uruguay, and southwestward across interior Brazil eastward to eastern Pará, Mato Grosso, and eastern Rondônia, across Paraguay southward to central Argentina (to northern La Pampa) and west to central Bolivia (Cochabamba and eastern La Paz)

ranges.Atrichornis clamosus: southwestern Australia (coastal heaths east of Albany)
ranges.Climacteris affinis: arid southern Western Australia eastward to ranges of central Australia, and eastern South Australia (western edge of Flinders Ranges), and southwestern Queenslandsouthward to southeastern South Australia
ranges.Climacteris erythrops: southeastern Australia (southeastern Queensland to Wombat Ranges, central Victoria)
ranges.Climacteris rufus: southwestern Australia (southwestern Western Australia eastward to Eyre Peninsula)
ranges.Sericulus chrysocephalus: eastern Australia (Clarke-Connors Range, Gladstone to eastern New South Wales, just north of Sydney)

ranges.Cinnyris chalcomelas: lowland coastal thornscrub in southern Somalia and eastern Kenya
ranges.Cinnyris pembae: lowland coastal forest, coastal rag scrub, plantations, and gardens, on Pemba Island (off northeastern Tanzania)
ranges.Cinnyris bouvieri: patchy in lowland to submontane forest edge, savanna woodland, wooded grassland, and plantations, from central Cameron and adjacent southeastern Nigeria eastward to Uganda and far western Kenya, and southward to northern Angola, southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northwestern Zambia
ranges.Cinnyris osea: patch, in bushy riversides, valleys and savannas of eastern Cameroon, southwestern Chad (Lake Chad), Central African Republic, southwestern Sudan, far northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, southwestern South Sudan, and northwestern Uganda, and disjunctly Syria and Israel to Türkiye and Arabia (eastward to Oman)

ranges.Cinnyris hellmayri: scrub in wadis and hillsides in the western Arabian Peninsula from northern Saudi Arabia southward to Yemen and western Oman
ranges.Cinnyris coccinigastrus: lowland to foothill forest edge, secondary forest, dry thornscrub, savanna, riverine woodland, plantations, and gardens, from Senegambia eastward to southern South Sudan and Uganda, and southward to northwestern Angola, central Democratic Republic of the Congo, and far northern Tanzania

ranges.Cinnyris rufipennis: local in foothill to submontane undisturbed primary forest in Udzungwa Mountains (south-central Tanzania)

ranges.Cinnyris fuscus: lowland semiarid coastal plain, acacia scrub, and gardens, from southwestern Angola and Namibia southward to southwestern Botswana and western and central South Africa; some irruptive movements
ranges.Cinnyris ursulae: foothill to submontane primary and secondary forest, and forest edge, in highlands of southwestern Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea)
ranges.Cinnyris batesi: patchy in lowland to foothill primary forest, cultivation with tall trees, and secondary growth, from Liberia eastward through southern Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and southward to northwestern Angola and far northwestern Zambia
ranges.Cinnyris cupreus: lowland to montane savanna, open woodland, swamps, mangroves, and gardens, from southwestern Mauritania and Senegal eastward to western Ethiopia, and southward through Gabon, western Kenya, and western Tanzania, to western Angola, northern Botswana, northern Zimbabwe, and central Mozambique; partially migratory in West Africa

ranges.Cinnyris teysmanni: Tanahjampea, Kalao, Bonerate, Kalaotoa, and Madu islands
ranges.Cinnyris idenburgi: northwestern New Guinea and Sepik Ramu

ranges.Chloropsis moluccensis: lowland to foothill broadleaf evergreen and mixed deciduous forest, forest edge, secondary growth, and rural gardens, from northeastern India (southern Assam and southern Arunachal Pradesh) and far northeastern Bangladesh eastward to south-central China and southeastern Asia, and southward to Sumatra, Borneo, and some satellite islands

ranges.Chloropsis flavipennis: central and southern Philippines (Cebu, Leyte, and Mindanao)
ranges.Chloropsis palawanensis: southwestern Philippines (Balabac, Busuanga, Palawan, and Calamian)

ranges.Irena tweeddalii: southern Philippines (Palawan, Busuanga, Balabac, Culion, and Calamian)
ranges.Irena puella: Western and northern Eastern Ghats of Peninsular India, eastern Nepal to northern Myanmar, Andaman Islands, southeastern Asia, Malayan Peninsula, and Greater Sundas

ranges.Urocynchramus pylzowi: mountains of western China and eastern Tibet

ranges.Sporopipes squamifrons: lowland to foothill dry savanna, thornscrub, open mopane woodland, arid Karoo, and gardens, from western and southern Angola eastward to southern Zambia and Zimbabwe, and southward to northern and central South Africa
ranges.Philetairus socius: lowland to foothill arid open country with scattered trees and bare ground, in Namibia, southern Botswana, and northwestern and north-central South Africa
ranges.Pseudonigrita cabanisi: patchy in foothill dry thornscrub and acacia savanna in southern Ethiopia southward to northeastern Tanzania
ranges.Pseudonigrita arnaudi: lowland and foothill open dry woodland from southwest Sudan and South Sudan eastward to southern Ethiopia and western Somalia, southward to northern and central Tanzania

ranges.Ploceus sanctithomae: highlands of São Tomé (Gulf of Guinea)

ranges.Ploceus aureonucha: local in lowland forest and secondary forest with tall emergent trees in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and adjacent western Uganda

ranges.Ploceus albinucha: patchily distributed in lowland and foothill evergreen forest and farmbush from southern Sierra Leone to southwestern Ghana, and from southern Nigeria, Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to northwestern Republic of Congo and southwestern Central African Republic, and from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to western Uganda

ranges.Ploceus olivaceiceps: patchy in lowland to submontane open miombo woodland from southwestern Tanzania southward to northern Mozambique, Malawi, and adjacent southeastern Zambia, and disjunctly in southern Mozambique
ranges.Ploceus nicolli: montane cloudforest in the Usambara, Uluguru (rare or extirpated?), and Udzungwa Mountains, Tanzania
ranges.Ploceus capensis: lowland to submontane savanna, grassland, Fynbos, coastal thickets, farmbush, gardens, and urban parks, in South Africa, Lesotho, and western Eswatini; occasional dispersal to adjacent southern Namibia
ranges.Ploceus temporalis: patchy and local in lowland to foothill rank grassland and riverine vegetation from central and northeastern Angola eastward to southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northwestern Zambia
ranges.Ploceus vitellinus: lowland and foothill dry savanna and arid scrub from southern Mauritania eastward through the Sahel to central Sudan, Ethiopia, and Somalia, southward to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and northern and central Tanzania
ranges.Ploceus spekei: foothill to montane savanna, open woodland, brushy scrub, and urban gardens, from Ethiopia and Somalia southward to southwestern Kenya and northeastern Tanzania
ranges.Ploceus spekeoides: foothill wooded and swampy and papyrus swamp in east-central Uganda; some seasonal dispersal
ranges.Ploceus aurantius: lowland and foothill riverine corridors, mangroves, coastal lagoons, and papyrus swamps from Sierra Leone eastward to western Central African Republic, and southward through Gabon to northwestern Angola, and from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to Lake Victoria in southern Uganda, western Kenya, and northwestern Tanzania

ranges.Ploceus bannermani: foothill to montane forest edge, degraded forest, and open scrub, in southeastern Nigeria and southwestern Cameroon
ranges.Ploceus nigrimentus: disjunctly in foothill open bushy savanna from southeastern Gabon, south-central Republic of the Congo, and adjacent southwestern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and in northeastern and west-central Angola
ranges.Ploceus baglafecht: patchy in lowland to montane shrubby or lightly wooded areas, marsh, forest edge, and gardens, from eastern Nigeria and Cameroon eastward to Eritrea and Ethiopia, and southward through eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and central Kenya to southwestern Tanzania, northeastern Zambia, and northern Malawi

ranges.Ploceus weynsi: lowland to foothill forest edge, lakeshore woodland; and secondary growth, from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and southern Uganda southward to northwestern Tanzania; in erratic wandering has reached western Kenya and northern Republic of the Congo
ranges.Ploceus xanthopterus: lowland and foothill wetlands with reedbeds or papyrus from southern Tanzania to Malawi, and from southeastern Angola, northeastern Namibia, and northern Botswana eastward to Mozambique, thence southward to coastal eastern South Africa
ranges.Ploceus castaneiceps: lowland to foothill swampy grassland, reeds, and brush in southeastern Kenya and northeastern Tanzania
ranges.Ploceus dichrocephalus: patchy in lowland to foothill savanna, riverine bush, acacia thornscrub, and semi-desert in southern Ethiopia, far northeastern Kenya, and southwestern Somalia
ranges.Ploceus holoxanthus: local in lowland reedbeds, riverine vegetation, and bamboo in eastern Tanzania (the lower Wami River, the Ruvu River, Lake Tagalala, and the Rufiji River)
ranges.Ploceus burnieri: lowland reedbeds in seasonally flooded grassland of Kilombero River floodplain (south-central Tanzania)
ranges.Ploceus heuglini: patchy in lowland to foothill wooded dry savanna, coastal thickets, secondary scrub, farmbush, and villages, from Senegambia eastward to southern Chad and Central African Republic, and disjunctly from southern South Sudan and northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to western Kenya; some seasonal dispersal

ranges.Ploceus xanthops: lowland to montane tall grass, brushy grassland, forest margins, and riverine vegetation, from southern Gabon eastward through southern and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to Uganda and southwestern Kenya, and southward to far northern Namibia, northern Botswana, and eastern South Africa
ranges.Ploceus katangae: patchy in lowland wetlands with reedbeds and papyrus from southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to northwestern Zambia
ranges.Ploceus bojeri: lowland to foothill coastal palm savanna, and riverine vegetation, in southern Somalia and central and eastern Kenya, and historically southeastern Ethiopia
ranges.Ploceus subaureus: lowland and foothill coastal plain, riverine marsh, and floodplain from eastern Kenya southward through Malawi and Mozambique to Eswatini and coastal southeastern South Africa
ranges.Ploceus galbula: lowland to submontane savanna, arid coastal plain, cultivation, and gardens, from eastern Sudan and Eritrea eastward to southwestern and southern Arabian Peninsula, and southward to southern Ethiopia and northern Somalia; introduced to western Red Sea coast and central Saudi Arabia

ranges.Ploceus ruweti: local in foothill riverine acacia and flooded savanna at Lake Tshangalele and Kiubo Falls on Lufira River (southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo)
ranges.Ploceus ocularis: patchy in lowland to montane woodland, bushy savanna, and gardens, from southwestern Nigeria and Cameroon eastward (avoiding Congolian rainforest) to southeastern Ethiopia and Kenya, and southward to southern Angola, northeastern Namibia, and northern Botswana, and through southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia to southern Mozambique, Eswatini, and south-eastern South Africa
ranges.Ploceus reichardi: local and patchy in lowland to foothill papyrus swamp and lakeshore reedbeds in western Tanzania and far northeastern Zambia
ranges.Ploceus golandi: local in lowland miombo woodland and coastal forest in southeastern Kenya
ranges.Ploceus luteolus: lowland to foothill acacia savanna, cultivation fringe, and gardens, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to Sudan, Eritrea, and Ethiopia, and southward to northern Cameroon, northern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, and northeastern Tanzania

ranges.Ploceus subpersonatus: lowland coastal swamp-forest, palm savanna, beach scrub, and mangroves from Gabon southward to Cabinda (northwestern Angola) and adjacent Democratic Republic of the Congo
