ranges.Crithagra striolata: montane forest, alpine moorland, and bamboo thickets in three disjunct areas: Eritrea, southern South Sudan, and Ethiopia; and from eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, Burundi to western Uganda, and from northeastern Uganda to central Kenya and southward to northern and south-central Tanzania
ranges.Crithagra whytii: foothill to montane understory in evergreen and riparian forest, secondary growth, and bracken-briar, from southern Tanzania, northeastern Zambia, and northern Malawi
ranges.Crithagra burtoni: undergrowth of montane forest, alpine grassland, and lightly wooded heath in four disjunct areas: southeastern Nigeria, western Cameroon, and Bioko, Gulf of Guinea; northwestern Angola; from eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to western Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, and northwestern Tanzania; and from northeastern Uganda eastward to northern Kenya and southward to northern Tanzania
ranges.Crithagra melanochroa: foothill to montane forest and brushy scrub in Iringa and Njombe highlands (southern Tanzania)
ranges.Crithagra rufobrunnea: lowland forest and plantations on São Tomé, Príncipe and adjacent Caroço Island, Gulf of Guinea
ranges.Crithagra leucoptera: lowland to foothill fynbos, protea thickets, semiarid scrub, and open woodland, in southwestern South Africa
ranges.Crithagra mennelli: patchy in lowland to montane dry woodland, miombo woodland, coastal forest, and eucalypt plantations, from eastern Angola, southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Tanzania southward to Zimbabwe and Mozambique; nomadic post-breeding
ranges.Crithagra canicapilla: patchily distributed in wooded savanna, farmbush, and montane dry forest from Guinea and Sierra Leone eastward to eastern Nigeria and Cameroon, and from southern Chad, Central African Republic, and southern South Sudan to northeastern Uganda and western Kenya; partly migratory in non-breeding season
ranges.Crithagra gularis: patchy in lowland to submontane scrub, savanna and miombo, and Fynbos from central Angola and northeastern Namibia eastward to northwestern Mozambique, then southward through Zimbabwe and northeast Botswana to eastern and southern South Africa, avoiding Namib and Kalahari deserts; partially migratory in non-breeding season
ranges.Crithagra striatipectus: patchy and local in foothill to submontane open woodland, shrubby escarpment, and wooded grassland, from Ethiopia and eastern South Sudan southward to western Kenya and adjacent eastern Uganda
ranges.Crithagra reichardi: foothill to submontane miombo and teak woodland from central and western Tanzania and southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo southward to Zambia, Malawi, and disjunctly in northern Mozambique
ranges.Crithagra tristriata: foothill to montane scrub, juniper woodland, rocky hillsides, gardens, and urban parks, in Eritrea, northern and central Ethiopia, and northern Somalia
ranges.Crithagra menachensis: foothill to montane dry scrub, rocky hillsides, stony plateaus, and in villages and towns, in southwestern Saudi Arabia, western Yemen, and far western Oman
ranges.Crithagra ankoberensis: submontane to montane cliffs and escarpments with vertical bare rock faces, open highland grassland, and stunted tree-heath, in northern and central Ethiopia
ranges.Crithagra totta: lowland to submontane fynbos, protea thickets, coastal scrub, woodland, and pine or eucalypt plantations, in southwestern South Africa; some altitudinal dispersal
ranges.Crithagra symonsi: submontane to montane heath, scrub, and highland grassland in east-central South Africa and Lesotho
ranges.Linaria flavirostris: low Arctic to temperate northwestern and montane central Palearctic in open areas: northern and central British Isles, western and northern Scandinavia; disjunctly Caucasus and south-central and northeastern Türkiye eastward through south-central Russia, northern Kazakhstan, northern and western Xinjiang (northwestern China), and Mongolia, in south to northwestern Iran, central Afghanistan through Altai region, northwestern Himalayas eastward to Nepal, Tibet, Qinghai, and Gansu (north-central China); winters to lower elevations and southward
ranges.Linaria cannabina: open lowland woodland and fields (alpine meadows in south) of British Isles, southern Scandinavia eastward to Altai region (south-central Russia), northern Xinjiang (northwestern China), and far western Mongolia, in south to Madeira and Canary Islands, Morocco to northern Libya, throughout Mediterranean to Türkiye, Cyprus, and the Levant, through Caucasus, Iran, and northern Afghanistan to eastern Kazakhstan; makes short-distance movements in winter
ranges.Linaria yemenensis: foothill to montane rocky scree, wadis with thornscrub, acacia scrub, juniper woodland, and plantations, in southwestern Saudi Arabia and western Yemen
ranges.Linaria johannis: foothill to montane arid plateaus, juniper woodland, thickets, scrub, and olive groves, in northern Somalia
ranges.Acanthis flammea: breeds Greenland and Iceland eastward to northeastern Russia, and Alaska to islands of far northeastern and southeastern Canada; winters to south
ranges.Loxia megaplaga: cordillera central of Dominican Republic and adjacent Haiti
ranges.Loxia leucoptera: conifer forest of subarctic to northern temperate Holarctic: eastern Scandinavia through Russia to Sea of Okhotsk, southward through south-central Russia, northeastern Mongolia, and probably Heilongjiang (far northeastern China); Alaska and Canada (except northern), Rocky Mountains and northern tier of contiguous USA; may winter irruptively southward
ranges.Loxia pytyopsittacus: coniferous forest of northeastern Europe to western Siberia
ranges.Loxia sinesciuris: South Hills and Albion Mountains of south-central Idaho (northwestern USA)
ranges.Loxia curvirostra: conifer forest of subarctic to subtropical Holarctic: British Isles, Scandinavia (except far north) eastward across Russia to Sea of Okhotsk, Sakhalin, and Kuril Islands (southeastern Russia), Hokkaido to central Honshu (northern to central Japan), North Korea, in south through Iberian Peninsula, Morocco to Tunisia (northwestern to north-central Africa), eastward through Mediterranean, Türkiye, Caucasus, Altai of eastern Kyrgyzstan, eastern Kazakhstan, northwestern Xinjiang (northwestern China), southern and central Mongolia to Heilongjiang and Hebei (northeastern China); disjunctly west-central to eastern Himalayas, southeastern Tibet, Qinghai, and Gansu to northwestern Yunnan; southern Vietnam; Luzon (northern Philippines); southeastern Alaska eastward to Newfoundland (northeastern Canada), southward to northern Baja California (northwestern Mexico), Rocky and Appalachian mountains, southward through Nicaragua; may winter irruptively southward
ranges.Chrysocorythus mindanensis: southern Philippines (Mount Katanglad and Mount Apo on Mindanao)
ranges.Chrysocorythus estherae: montane forest, humid montane grasslands above treeline and heather-dominated meadows with scattered scrub in the mountains of northwestern Sumatra, locally in Java, and in central Sulawesi
ranges.Carduelis citrinella: montane coniferous forest of southern Europe
ranges.Carduelis caniceps: lowland to montane open conifer, deciduous, and mixed woodland, heath, steppe grassland, scrub, cultivation, parks, and gardens from south-central Siberia, eastern Mongolia, and northwestern China southward to eastern Iran, and eastward through Himalayas from northern Pakistan to Nepal; downslope and erratic post-breeding dispersal
ranges.Carduelis carduelis: lowland to submontane open deciduous and mixed woodland, heath, steppe grasslands, cultivation, parks, and gardens from British Isles and southern Scandinavia eastward to Ural Mountains (Russia), and southward to Madeira and Canary Islands, northwestern Africa, Mediterranean Europe, Nile Valley (Egypt), Levant, and western Iran; northern populations migrate to southern Europe and Middle East; introduced widely, including Azores and Cabo Verde, southeastern Australia, New Zealand, Wisconsin (USA), Bermuda, Uruguay, and east-central Argentina
ranges.Serinus canaria: Azores, Madeira, and western Canary Islands
ranges.Serinus serinus: open woodland of southern Palearctic region
ranges.Serinus pusillus: mountains of Türkiye to western China; winters to Israel
ranges.Serinus syriacus: breeds mountains of Lebanon and Syria; winters to Türkiye and northwestern Iraq
ranges.Serinus nigriceps: foothill to montane moorland, highland grassland, often with giant heath and giant lobelias, euphorbia thickets, and cultivation edges, in northern and central Ethiopia
ranges.Serinus alario: lowland and foothill arid scrub, rocky outcrops, vleis, and gardens from central and southern Namibia southward to southwestern South Africa, and eastward to central South Africa (Northern Cape, Eastern Cape) and Lesotho; undertakes nomadic and irruptive movements
ranges.Serinus canicollis: montane forest, moorland, thornscrub and Fybos from eastern Zimbabwe and adjacent Mozambique to South Africa (southward to KwaZulu-Natal and Eswatini, and westward to Western Cape); downslope wandering in non-breeding season
ranges.Serinus flavivertex: montane forest and alpine moorland in highlands from Eritrea, Ethiopia, and South Sudan southward to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and eastward to Kenya, thence southward to southern Tanzania and Malawi, and in west-central Angola; downslope wandering in non-breeding season

ranges.Spinus lawrencei: breeds southern California and northwestern Baja; winters to Texas and northern Sonora
ranges.Spinus tristis: breeds in weedy and grassy fields, orchards, bushy areas, and gardens from southern British Columbia eastward to southwestern Newfoundland (southwestern to southeastern Canada) southward through southern California and to northern Louisiana and Georgia; winters southward to northern Baja California and northern (northwestern Mexico), Veracruz (eastern Mexico), and southern Florida
ranges.Spinus psaltria: varied woodland, scrub, and forest-edge habitats and agricultural fields from western USA, from central Washington to southern Wyoming and southward to southern Texas, Baja California, and through mountains of Mexico to northern Nicaragua, also in Yucatan Peninsula, southwestern Costa Rica and Panama, Sierra de Perijá, Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, central Venezuela, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward along the Andes of Colombia to northern Ecuador and from southern Ecuador to north-central Peru (to Ancash)
ranges.Spinus spinus: breeds northern Palearctic; winters southward to Mediterranean region, China, and Ryukyu Islands
ranges.Spinus atriceps: coniferous forest of southern Mexico (Chiapas) and western Guatemala
ranges.Spinus pinus: breeds open coniferous forest, mixed coniferous-deciduous forest, and woodland from southern Alaska eastward to Newfoundland and Labrador (northeastern Canada), southward in western USA to mountains in northern Baja California (northwestern Mexico), throughout mountains of western and central USA and Mexico southward to western Guatemala, and northeastern USA (Minnesota to Maine); winters irregularly across the Great Plains and eastern USA southward to central Mexico
ranges.Spinus notatus: forest and edge of hills and mountains in Mexico southward from southern Sonora in the west and southern Tamaulipas in the east, southward through southern Mexico (except northern Yucatan Peninsula), Guatemala, west-central Belize, and Honduras to northern Nicaragua
ranges.Spinus cucullatus: northeastern Colombia, northern Venezuela, and southwestern Guyana; local and threatened
ranges.Spinus barbatus: central Chile and southern Argentina to Tierra del Fuego and Falkland Islands
ranges.Spinus olivaceus: east slope of Andes of southeastern Ecuador to Peru and western Bolivia (La Paz and Cochabamba)
ranges.Spinus spinescens: Andean grassland in paramos from northwestern Venezuela southward to the high Andes of northeastern Colombia, including the Sierra de Perijá and Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, and in the western and central Andes of Colombia southward to far northern Ecuador (Carchi)
ranges.Spinus yarrellii: northern Venezuela; interior northeastern Brazil (Ceará to Bahia)
ranges.Spinus xanthogastrus: highly disjunct in humid to semi-humid woodland, forest borders, and scrub in the mountains of Costa Rica and western Panama, in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela, and in the Andes of western Venezuela southward along all Andes of Colombia to the western Andes of Ecuador and far northern Peru, and in the Andes of far southeastern Peru and Bolivia (to western Santa Cruz)
ranges.Spinus siemiradzkii: southwestern Ecuador including Isla Puná, and far northwestern Peru (Tumbes)
ranges.Spinus crassirostris: montane shrubby steppe, scattered woodland (including Polylepis), and shrubland from the western Andes of north-central Peru (Ancash) southward to western Bolivia and adjacent Chile, and from the Andes of central Bolivia (Cochabamba) southward to northwestern Argentina (to Mendoza) and adjacent central Chile
ranges.Spinus atratus: Andes of central Peru to northern Chile and Argentina
ranges.Spinus uropygialis: Andes of central Peru to northwestern Argentina and northern Chile
ranges.Spinus magellanicus: disjunctly in dry to humid montane woodland and scrub, and open areas with trees, in tepuis of southern Venezuela, far northern Brazil (Roraima), and adjacent Guyana, in the central Andes of Colombia and locally in the western Andes southward through Peru, where also reaches the Pacific coast, to far northern Chile, across Bolivia and in the Cerrado, Caatinga, and Atlantic Forest of central and eastern Brazil, from Tocantins southward to central Argentina (to Río Negro)

ranges.Rhynchophanes mccownii: breeds western Canada to northwestern USA; winters to northwestern Mexico
ranges.Plectrophenax hyperboreus: breeds Bering Sea islands; winters to coastal Alaska and Aleutians
ranges.Plectrophenax nivalis: breeds Holarctic, from Greenland and Arctic islands and coasts eastward to Chukchi Peninsula and Kamchatka, and Aleutians, Alaska, and northern Canada to Ellesmere Island; winters to central Eurasia and central North America
ranges.Calcarius lapponicus: breeds Greenland and Scandinavia to northeastern Siberia, including High Arctic islands, southward to Kamchatka, and Aleutians, Alaska, and northern Canadian Arctic eastward to Ellesmere Island; winters to central Eurasia and central USA
ranges.Calcarius pictus: breeds Alaska and western Canada; winters in south-central USA
ranges.Calcarius ornatus: breeds prairies of central North America; winters southwestern USA to northern Mexico

ranges.Fringillaria flaviventris: open woodland of Sahel zone and disjunctly eastern and southern Africa: southern Mauritania to northern Eritrea and far northern Ethiopia; southern Democratic Republic of the Congo and far southern South Sudan through eastern Africa, southward through South Africa (except southwestern)

ranges.Fringillaria affinis: mesic woodland of Sahel zone and northeastern Africa, from Senegal, far southern Mauritania to northern Guinea and eastward to western and southern Ethiopia, northern Uganda, and western Kenya
ranges.Fringillaria capensis: open rocky shrubland of southern Africa: southwestern Angola eastward to western Mozambique, southward through southern South Africa
ranges.Fringillaria impetuani: southwestern African succulent and grassy Karoo: coastal central Angola to Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, and western and central South Africa
ranges.Fringillaria socotrana: densely vegetated rocky slopes of montane Socotra; winters to lower elevations

ranges.Fringillaria goslingi: foothill to submontane arid scrub, mesic woodland, lightly wooded savanna, bare or sandy ground, short grassland, and degraded pasture, from Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to eastern Sudan and northeastern South Sudan, and southward to Cameroon and Central African Republic; partial migrant with rains, and nomadic wandering
ranges.Fringillaria tahapisi: rocky hillsides of subtropical to tropical northeastern to southern Africa: Gabon eastward to northeastern Somalia and Socotra, and southern Arabian Peninsula southward through South Africa
ranges.Schoeniclus siemsseni: mountains of central China (southern Shaanxi, southeastern Gansu, and northeastern Sichuan)

ranges.Schoeniclus yessoensis: far east-central Palearctic marshes, patchily in far eastern Mongolia, Heilongjiang (northeastern China), far southeastern Ussuriland (southeastern Russia), and Honshu to Kyushu (central to southern Japan); winters central Honshu to Kyushu (central and southern Japan), Korean Peninsula, and coastal east-central China

ranges.Schoeniclus schoeniclus: subarctic to temperate Palearctic marshes, from British Isles, Scandinavia, and northwestern Russia through Sea of Okhotsk, Kamchatka, Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin (eastern Russia); in south through Iberian Peninsula and northwestern Morocco, eastward through Mediterranean, Türkiye, Caucasus, northern and south-central Iran, Turkmenistan, and Tajikistan to northern Xinjiang (northwestern China), western Mongolia, northeastern China, and Hokkaido and northern Honshu (northern Japan); in winter makes short-range southward movements to wider habitat range

ranges.Cassiculus melanicterus: Pacific lowlands of western Mexico (southeastern Sonora) to southeastern Guatemala and northwestern El Salvador

ranges.Icterus melanopsis: Cuba including Isla de la Juventud

ranges.Icterus dominicensis: Hispaniola, including Gonâve, Tortue, and Île-a-Vache

ranges.Pseudoleistes guirahuro: eastern Paraguay to southern Brazil, Uruguay, and northern Argentina

ranges.Poecilostreptus cabanisi: cloudforest of southern Mexico (Chiapas) and adjacent Guatemala
ranges.Poecilostreptus palmeri: humid foothills of eastern Panama to northwestern Ecuador (Pichincha)
ranges.Stilpnia larvata: humid forest from southeastern Mexico southward along the Caribbean slope of Central America and the Pacific slope of Costa Rica and Panama to northwestern Colombia; in interior Colombia eastward to the upper Magdalena Valley in Tolima, and west of the Andes southward to northwestern Ecuador
ranges.Stilpnia nigrocincta: southeastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, Guyana, northern Bolivia, and western Brazil
ranges.Stilpnia cyanicollis: humid lowland and montane forest, gallery forest, and woodland in the coastal mountains of northwestern Venezuela, Sierra de Perijá, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward to northern Peru north of the Río Marañón; in western Ecuador and adjacent southwestern Colombia down to the lowlands, the eastern Andes of Peru south of the Río Marañón, southward to central Bolivia, the Cerrado and southern Amazon basin of Brazil (southeastern Pará and northern Tocantins southward to southern Mato Grosso), and adjacent northeastern Bolivia
ranges.Stilpnia cyanoptera: mountains of northern Colombia including Santa Marta region to northeastern Venezuela
ranges.Stilpnia whitelyi: tepuis of southern Venezuela (in Amazonas and Bolívar), adjacent northern Brazil, and southwestern Guyana (Mount Twek-quay)
ranges.Stilpnia viridicollis: humid to dry montane forest and scrub in the Andes from southern Ecuador southward to northern Peru and along the eastern Andes from northeastern Peru southward to western Bolivia
ranges.Stilpnia phillipsi: Andes of eastern Peru (Cerros del Sira in eastern Huánuco)
ranges.Stilpnia peruviana: lowlands of southeastern Brazil (Rio de Janeiro to Santa Catarina)
ranges.Stilpnia heinei: mountains of northern Colombia to northern Venezuela and northern Ecuador
ranges.Stilpnia argyrofenges: humid montane forest in the eastern Andes from southeastern Ecuador southward to northeastern Peru and in southeastern Peru southward to south-central Bolivia
ranges.Stilpnia preciosa: eastern Paraguay to southeastern Brazil, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
ranges.Stilpnia meyerdeschauenseei: east slope of Andes of far southeastern Peru (Puno)
ranges.Stilpnia vitriolina: arid scrub of western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador
ranges.Stilpnia cucullata: scrub to forest at all elevations, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, and Grenada (southern Lesser Antilles)
ranges.Stilpnia cayana: open and semi-open areas near semi-humid to dry forest, gallery forest, woodland savanna, white-sand forest, campo grasslands, and gardens and parks from northeastern Colombia eastward to northern and eastern Venezuela, northern Guianas, and northeastern Brazil westward to the llanos of northeastern Colombia; and in the Cerrado, Caatinga, and Atlantic Forest regions from northeastern Brazil southward to northern Paraná, southern Mato Grosso, northern Bolivia, southeasternmost Peru, eastern Paraguay, and northeasternmost Argentina; also isolated in the Rio Mayo valley of northern Peru
